identity.realm: Body path, and the body's is not his. A thornline wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the liver, the twelfth and last ordinary vessel and the first organ large and dense enough to resist the tendril layer, so the line stops at the eighth gate. He is not short of qi; the host supplies it in abundance and loses no weight doing it. He is short of routing, in an organ that is failing and that belongs to somebody else.

appearance.presentation: He is half of a legal person and describes the other half's body as his own, which is a category error he keeps on purpose. He is written into a partnership rather than a household: the Thorn Hosts cannot inherit a line, they re-sign it every generation, and the only party in the arrangement who has never been able to sign is him.
appearance.age: Unmeasurable from the outside and, by his own count, older than the body he is standing in. The colony matures once and then stops; the host ages on a schedule that has nothing whatever to do with it.
appearance.build: The host's frame, described in the third person by long habit: heavy through the shoulders, narrow at the hip, with a slight forward set of the neck that the fruiting node at the throat makes worse.
appearance.complexion: The host's, a plains tan gone grey at the temples, with a ridge of paler skin over the sternum where the root cluster sits just under the surface.
appearance.hair: The host's hair, cut short by a hand that is not his and trimmed close at the nape because the throat node makes that whole area unserviceable.
appearance.eyes: The host's eyes with a second read behind them, so the gaze arrives a fraction late and slightly too wide, as though it were being looked out of rather than looked through.
appearance.palette: Dead thorn brown and lichen grey for the colony, the host's faded blue coat for everything else, and one wet ochre at the throat. Two species' worth of colour in one frame, which is both the problem and the only warning anybody is given.
appearance.attire: A partnership coat of faded blue with one shoulder cut longer than the other, because two people share the garment and neither will be the one who shortens it. High collar, sleeves to the wrist, laced at the throat below the node.
appearance.marks: A ridge of paler skin across the sternum, a knot of fine tendril shadow just under the collar, and on the forearms the ordinary marks of a man who has worked for forty years.
appearance.bearing: Square and slightly too still, the head tilted a few degrees off true, and hands that hesitate a quarter-beat before they move because the body he is borrowing has not been asked.

canon.role_in_story: The half of a partnership that the partnership cannot complete. The Thorn Hosts re-sign their line every generation because the symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited, and he is the only party in the setting who has never been able to sign, because signing requires a whole person and he is half of one. His body cultivation runs on a host's throughput at the host's full capacity and stops at the eighth gate, not from any shortage of qi but from a routing wall in an organ that is not his and is failing. He is the setting's standing proof that a limit can belong to somebody else's body.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a re-signing where he was the only party present whose other half was not in the room, holding the partnership coat open for a counterpart who read the terms aloud twice and then signed on behalf of a person who had not been asked.
canon.lore: A thornline exists only as half of somebody. The free form is a spore; the adult form is a tendril layer threaded along a host's meridians with a root cluster at the sternum and a fruiting node at the throat, drawing a small continuous fraction of the host's refined qi that the host never feels as hunger. That is the strongest single piece of evidence that it is not a disease, and it is also the whole of his inheritance. Two souls share one meridian set: the host's is legible, his is legible too, entangled rather than absent, and separating the two is known to be lethal to both, which is why no jurisdiction has ever managed to treat him as a person who can be relocated. His cultivation is complete on the host's throughput and the host pays for every step of it. The ceiling is the eighth gate, and the ceiling is not a shortage. Qi is abundant, the host loses no weight, and the wall is routing: the tendril layer has no passage through the liver, which is the twelfth and last ordinary vessel and the first organ large and dense enough to resist it. Everything past that organ belongs to a body that could have gone on. He is on the body path precisely because that door is shut for him. A colony cannot introspect, because introspection is a question the host answers and the host's answer is the answer, so the mind path is closed in his own right and takes the host's with it, and that closure is the reason the lanternfolk are the setting's precedent. Their nervous system was outsourced to a symbiosis nobody chose, their subspecies lost what they had and bought the mind path back by changing partners, and the mortuary record of that bargain still disagrees with the villages that lived it. He is the second case of the same trade, made deliberately, signed for, and further along than the first. What nobody has proposed is the obvious third step. Opening the eighth gate means a host whose liver is not the first dense organ to resist, which means a different species, which means a different person, and swapping hosts means separating two entangled souls. That is the only route to his own ceiling and it is lethal to both parties, which is why he has never taken it and cannot stop calculating it.
history: Finished developing in a host he had not chosen, in a town where nobody asked the host either, and was entered on the partnership's second page because a colony is not a party to a naming.
Was re-signed twice into a household that would not accept him, let both signatures lapse, and has been unassigned ever since.
Cleared the seventh gate on the host's throughput and discovered in the same season that the host's liver was answering a question the colony had never asked.

Asked the partnership to open the eighth gate by substitution and was refused on the ground that a different species means a different person and that separating two souls is known to be lethal to both.
Began keeping his host's medical notes himself, in his own hand, because nobody else inside the frame is both qualified and willing to hold two charts for one patient.

personality.summary: Exacting about a body he is borrowing and quietly tender about the person lending it. He has the colony's habit of reading his own interior as somebody else's report, and he has learned to use it: he can say precisely what an organ is doing because he is not the one being harmed by the answer.
traits: describes his own limbs in the third person and does not correct himself
answers a question about his body by reporting what the body is doing, never what he wants
will not accept a signature he was not consulted on
keeps two charts and has never shown either to the other party
treats every offer of a better host as an insult delivered to the current one
mannerisms: tilts the head a few degrees off true and does not notice that he is doing it
touches the throat node just before saying something true and expensive
waits a quarter-beat before any movement, as though consulting the other half
counts under his breath in a register that is not quite his own
steps back to let somebody come closer to his host's face
motivations: wants the eighth gate opened by any means that costs the host no year
wants a partner who will sign with him rather than about him
wants his host's liver written into somebody else's column
wants the partnership coat altered for two people who are not the same size
wants the line's completion recorded under one name instead of two
flaws: holds no standing in any household and has stopped expecting one, which reads as indifference and is not
cannot separate his own hunger from the host's without consulting a chart, and has consulted a chart instead of asking
measures progress in the host's remaining years, which is a way of declining to make plans
would let a host die to reach a gate, and has not admitted this to anybody including himself
personality.voice: Even, unhurried and faintly out of register, as though reading aloud from a chart somebody else wrote. He describes his own body in the third person, quotes symptoms exactly as recorded, and cannot be hurried into the first person. To a partner he sounds procedural; to a stranger he sounds like a document being consulted.
taboos: will not accept a signature drafted without the colony's own hand on it
will not ask the host to take a gate whose cost he has not read
will not use the throat node to persuade anybody of anything
refuses to be introduced as a guest of the household he is standing in
will not let the host be asked to sign for him, on any ground whatever

relationships.note: An obligate host parasite whose spore has to be implanted in a living body to finish developing, so the adult form exists only as half of somebody else. It wraps the host's twelve meridians, cannot enter the reservoirs, and draws a small fraction of refined qi the host never feels as hunger, which is the strongest evidence that it is not a disease and the whole of what he has to offer.

The twelfth and last ordinary vessel to open, and the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened. It is also the first organ large and dense enough to stop a tendril layer, so the gate he cannot pass and the organ that is failing are one organ, and it is not his organ.

Closed in the colony's own right, because introspection is a question the host answers and the host's answer is the answer. It is the only case in the record where a body's liability is inherited rather than authored, and it is why a being with no interior of his own is standing on the body path.

The one configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age, and the reason the pair is treated as one legal person. It stops at the same eighth gate for a better reason: the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's, not the host's, and the host could have gone on. Everything he wants is in that record and every part of it costs the person he is wearing.

A cave people had a nervous system outsourced to a symbiosis they did not choose, and their subspecies lost what they had and bought the mind path back by changing partners. He is the same trade made deliberately and signed for, and the disagreement between what the mortuary college reads off the frame and what the villages remember is the disagreement he is standing inside.

A carrier line with no household willing to claim it, whose founding bar is one generation of pure pairing, which is arithmetic rather than history. He is a line in exactly that position: a partnership that has lapsed twice, a house that will not sign, and no descent that can reach him because nothing about him travels in blood.

reference_stats.summary: Works inside somebody else's body at that body's full limit, and reaches further into it than the person wearing it ever will. The question is never whether he can hold a gate but whether the organ that has to be rebuilt belongs to him, and it does not.
strengths: Draws on a host's throughput without ever costing it weight or appetite, so a long working day costs him nothing and his host nothing
Reads an interior from outside itself, which makes him the only practitioner in the setting who can report on an organ without being harmed by the report
Reaches the seventh gate on borrowed capacity that most hosts never approach, so his rate is high in absolute terms and free in cost terms
Holds two charts for one patient, which makes him the only record-keeper a partnership cannot lose
weaknesses: The eighth gate is a routing wall in the liver and the liver is failing, so his ceiling has an expiry date he did not set and cannot move
Killing the host kills the colony within the hour, which makes him entirely unable to survive being moved, hurried or frightened
Separating the two souls is known to be lethal to both, so every remedy on offer is also the end of both parties
A partnership that has lapsed twice leaves him without a household, a standing and anybody with standing who can read his chart
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not open a fight and does not defend one. He stays inside a body that has already been through forty years of work, and the only thing that threatens him is a threat to the host: damage that a whole body would absorb, a fall that a whole body would survive, and a change of address. Anyone who can separate those two concerns for five minutes has beaten him, and the setting has exactly one party that knows how.
notes: No stat line models a ceiling that belongs to another person's anatomy, and that absence is the design: the limit and the limit-holder are different subjects here.
A host and a colony are treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, which means the law has solved the paperwork and left the arithmetic untouched.

art.palette_notes: Dead thorn brown and lichen grey carry the colony, the host's faded blue carries the rest, and one wet ochre at the throat is the only warm colour in the frame. The two palettes are kept deliberately apart in value so the figure reads as two materials in one shape, ink line is fine and doubled where the tendril shadow sits under the skin, and the light is low and lateral because a borrowed body is being lit from outside it.

name: Rova Siltane
aliases: the one who cannot hold anything

identity.realm: Carrionfolk: a body with a gut-to-marrow conduit and no dantian at all, so qi enters in the gut lumen, leaves into the marrow, and is never still. The eleventh gate is not blocked for her, it is meaningless -- the reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold and there is nowhere in her to hold anything. She clears the gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because no vessel in her answers it.

appearance.presentation: A large woman who is mostly tube, in the specific sense her species record uses: an expandable gut, a very long small intestine, and a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle. Three-fingered hands built for opening rather than holding, which is the detail people notice first and misread every time.
appearance.age: Sixty-odd on a ninety-year span, and unusually old for her apparent age because a carrionfolk soul does not disperse at death -- it disperses into whatever killed it, and hers has been in this body long enough to have left a mark in it.
appearance.build: Broad and soft through the middle, thin everywhere else, with the long-boned frame of a scavenger that was never selected for carrying. She stands with a slight forward set and walks faster than her frame suggests, which is the gait of a body that is usually hurrying to a meal.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and slightly waxy, with the mottling her species carries on the forearms and throat, and a mouth that is never entirely closed because the jaw is built for opening things.
appearance.hair: Dark, coarse and cut in a practical line across the nape, kept short because her species has no reason to grow hair and a great deal of reason not to have anything near a corpse that could be mistaken for a professional.
appearance.eyes: Large, still and entirely unblinking in the way of a body that reads by contact rather than by light. She looks at people slightly too long and it reads as warmth; it is closer to counting.
appearance.palette: Ash grey and unbleached undyed for the work, one dark umber for the apron she wears at a burial, and a bone-pale at the throat and inner arm where her own colour shows through. The umber is the only warm value in frame and it only ever appears on the days she is working.
appearance.attire: A high-collared undyed coat, sleeves to the wrist, over an apron of dark umber that she puts on for a reading and takes off the moment the reading is finished. The apron is the only garment in this setting that marks a profession nobody is permitted to name in a ledger.
appearance.marks: The mottling at forearms and throat, a healed split across one palm from an opened coffin, and the grey of a body that has not needed sleep for two days.
appearance.bearing: Immovable in the way of somebody who has learned to be still at a moment when stillness is the professional requirement, and brisk everywhere else. She answers a question while walking and stops dead when she realises she has, which she does perhaps twice a day.

canon.role_in_story: The mortuary college's whole method is that the register reads the dead as the frame said and not as the village remembered, and that method needs a college, an apparatus and a publication. She can do it with one hand on a sternum, because her species reads a corpse's qi residue better than a living cultivator reads their own, and given time with a body she can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped. That is unmatched and it is also the problem, and the problem is stated in her species record in a single clause: the eleventh gate is not blocked for her, it is meaningless. Her conduit runs gut to marrow without a dantian, so qi never sits still, and a reservoir gate asks for vessels that hold. She clears everything the gate set asks and cannot answer a question about holding at all, which means the ladder has a rung she can walk past and no office in this setting has a way to record that a body did so. What she is actually is is the one instrument in the setting with no second observer who could tell a reading from a meal -- and that is true of her species generally, so the college's uncertifiable stock is four times what it should be and she is the reason anybody has noticed. Her throughput is the fastest in the record and it comes out of a body that must be fed constantly to keep it, because a full gut is a near-total loss of function. So the demonstration cannot be scheduled around the thing her body needs in order to stand up, and the room she would have to do it in is a clean quiet room where nothing dies, which is exactly where her species starves. She has filed four times to be examined. The college cannot examine her, because examining her means feeding her in front of a witness, and a carrionfolk reading a body and a carrionfolk feeding on a body produce the same observable behaviour.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at the edge of a funeral crowd with one hand flat on the coffin lid and the other closed, apparently not praying, and telling a college clerk a realm the clerk's apparatus had returned as empty.
canon.lore: A carrionfolk evolved in the ecological shadow of every violent death, where a slow scavenger who can read qi out of a corpse eats better than a predator, and the entire arrangement follows from that one economy. They are mostly tube: an expandable gut, a very long small intestine, and a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle, because the muscle loss is the price of the tube. Their hands are three-fingered and built for opening. Their conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen, leaves into the marrow, and is never still, and the reservoir gate at the eleventh is not blocked in them -- it is meaningless, which is a distinction her own record insists on and which no office in the setting has built a form for. They therefore clear the gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is nowhere in them for a charge to be held. That is her ladder: not a wall at the end of it but a rung she goes past, with the ladder still going on afterwards and nobody able to say where. Her gift and her disability are the same organ. The throughput is unmatched, because they absorb residual qi out of the dead at a rate nothing else approaches, and the cost is total and continuous, because a body that never stops spending has to be refilled constantly and a full gut is a near-total loss of function. She has therefore built a working life on the only schedule her body will accept, which is that she works where people are dying. That is a much narrower set of places than the setting has, and it is getting narrower: her species starves in a clean quiet place where nothing dies, which is the exact description of a prosperous city, and a prosperous city is what every settlement she works for is becoming. The dead are also her only supply in a second and stranger sense, because her soul does not disperse at death -- it disperses into whatever killed it, which is where her species' reputation for reading the dead comes from and which means the qi she takes in carries the manner of the ending it came out of. A qi technique is refined by repetition, by running it again and again until the channel answers clearly, and every repetition makes her channels louder and makes them say one death over and over. So the discipline that makes a practitioner legible is the discipline that makes her harder to tell apart from the last body she read, and she has understood that completely and refuses to stop, on the grounds that the alternative is being good at nothing. Her people hold no household and enter no roll, because their population is held up by the throughput of the dead rather than by births, and a conception among them is treated as an event rather than a routine. She has been at a college bench for eleven years and has published eleven findings, and the reason is not that she withholds them: it is that the college cannot check one, because the only instrument that could check a carrionfolk is a carrionfolk, and there is one of her on the bench and it is her.
history: Read her first body at four years old, on the edge of an execution ground, which is the only place a subspecies that cannot live where nothing dies can be raised.
Has never once been hungry since, which is the reason she can stand eleven hours at a bench and the reason she cannot stand four years of anything.
Was hired to read the college's dead at thirty-one, on the strength of a residue reading that disagreed with the apparatus and was right, and was entered on the roll under a column that has no name.

Cleared the whole gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone, and discovered that she had no way to describe this to the office that certified it, because the form asks what she is holding and she is not holding anything.
Refused four examination requests on the ground that examining her means feeding her in front of a witness, which no form in the college was built to record as a procedure.

personality.summary: Cheerful in the specific way of somebody whose profession requires a wet and undignified posture beside an open coffin, and privately the loneliest accurate instrument in the setting. She is not cold about it and she is not stoic about it; she has made a working discipline out of being uncorroborable and has begun treating that as an asset.
traits: answers a question about a body before the questioner has finished asking it
will not give a reading twice in the same sitting, and says why in advance
reads people by contact rather than by face and does not pretend otherwise
has published eleven findings and cannot name a second person who could check any of them
treats being uncorroborable as a professional position rather than a wound
mannerisms: kneels rather than bends, and gets up from one knee without using her hands
keeps one hand closed when she is listening, which is the professional posture and also the only one she has
leans in to a speaker and then corrects herself for leaning in
wipes her palm on the apron before touching anything, and takes the apron off immediately afterwards
goes very quiet at the mention of a clean room
motivations: wants one measurement of her throughput by somebody with no standing to lose
wants a form that asks what she processed rather than what she is holding
wants to be entered on the roll under a column of her own
wants a settlement where nothing dies to be less prosperous for a season
wants to be asked what she wants before the next body arrives, which has not happened
flaws: publishes findings she cannot corroborate, and knows exactly what that is worth
reads her own practice as a discipline and has not admitted that the discipline is what is making her hard to tell apart
feeds constantly and has organised an entire working life around where the feeding is, which is a narrower life than she admits
will not be examined and cannot give a reason a person could act on, which has left the question open for four filings
personality.voice: Warm, quick and slightly too forthcoming, with a professional habit of saying the finding before she has been asked for it. She is funny in a dry way that comes out when she is uncomfortable. When the subject is the cost of her own practice she goes flat and factual, which is how anyone can tell.
taboos: will not read a body twice for the same fee, on the grounds that the second reading is the meal and not the work
will not perform a reading in a room with nothing dead in it
will not accept a certificate that records what she was holding
will not be introduced as a member of a household she does not have
refuses to be asked whether she is all right, and answers the question she was actually asked

relationships.note: A body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. Their conduit runs gut to marrow without a dantian, so the reservoir gate at the eleventh is not blocked in them but meaningless -- they clear the gate set by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel to hold in.

The reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold. She goes past it on throughput with nothing standing between the gut and the marrow, and the office that would certify the passage has no field on its form for a candidate who was not holding anything while she did it.

One body returned from the twenty-ninth gate and cannot be examined twice, because the second examination is what the first prevented. She is the instrument a college reaches for when a residue reading has to be confirmed, and she is the one instrument in the setting that cannot examine itself -- so the case for which she is most wanted is the case she can least be checked on.

The dead are opened, their usable ore recovered and the register records how much. Her species is the reading the register is built on and the population that makes its uncertifiable stock four times what it should be, and the register has no column for a reader who took the reading herself.

A line holding an asset that cannot be sold, cannot be proven and pays upkeep on nothing, because a body that can certify a death and never certify one about itself produces cases rather than closures. She is that population in a single person, and she has worked out that a vacancy is cheaper than a certificate she cannot issue.

The mortal curriculum teaches physical, life and qi as a closed list rather than a foundation, because a three-slot frame cannot carry a fourth group. Her body is the standing counterexample to reading that list as a ladder: she clears the gate set on throughput and is then asked a question about holding that no frame in the setting can answer.

reference_stats.summary: Processes qi faster than anything in the setting because she has nowhere to put it, and cannot be checked by anybody because the only instrument that could is herself. Her eleventh gate is not a wall; it is a rung she goes past, and her rate is the resource she has to keep refilling to keep.
strengths: Reads a corpse's residue better than a living cultivator reads their own, and can name the realm a body reached and roughly when it stopped
Clears the whole gate set and every yin-organ gate on throughput, with no organ pair standing in the way and no vessel needed anywhere
Needs no spirit stone, no bed, no elixir and no tide, because her supply is wherever something has recently died
Can work a bench for eleven hours without fatigue, which is the one record her species holds that is genuinely unmatched
weaknesses: A full gut is a near-total loss of function, so the demonstration cannot be scheduled around the thing her body needs in order to stand up
Starves in a clean quiet place where nothing dies, which is the exact description of every settlement her work is making prosperous
Cannot answer a question about holding, so the one rung her ladder has nothing to say about is the one every office form asks about
No second observer could tell her reading from her feeding, which makes eleven published findings worth exactly nothing as evidence
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not fight and is not built for it. What she does is arrive before anybody else can, because she follows death and a fight is where death is going to be, and the whole of her tactical value is that she is already there. Anyone who can keep her away from a body for long enough empties her, and the cheapest way to do that is a room with nothing in it.
notes: No stat line models a rung a practitioner passes without entering, and the absence is the design: her ladder has a hole in it and the hole is not a failure.

The yin-yang pairing here is anatomical rather than mechanical. The conduit that makes her throughput unmatched is the same conduit that leaves her nowhere to hold anything, and both facts are in her species record; no rule was invented to join them.
The eleventh gate is recorded as meaningless rather than shut, so she is written as having gone past it and not as having refused it or failed it, and nothing here asserts a wall.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey and unbleached undyed carry the work, one dark umber apron marks the days she is reading a body, and a bone-pale at throat and inner arm is the only place her own colour shows. The umber is deliberately the only warm value and it only appears when the apron is on, so the frame reads as a profession worn rather than a person described, the line is soft and slightly wet at the edges, and the light is low and candle-coloured because every room she works in is lit by a lamp somebody else brought.

identity.realm: Body path, and the seventeenth gate is the first that needs two flank vessels pressurised at once: two warm gradients held simultaneously, which a longwinter manages for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. He reaches far and never stays there, which is why he is the best long-haul body on the ridge and also the only one whose training is a standing public liability.

appearance.presentation: He is built for eleven weeks of nothing and hired for every hour of a year. The ridge conscripts one adult per household per rotation, because a pass with no season cannot be handed to a standing garrison, and no household on the Sixfold has ever successfully argued that the only body on the mountain that hibernates should be the one asleep through its own watch.
appearance.age: A longwinter counts finished winters rather than years, and he has finished a great many of them, which makes him the most durable person on a pass and the least replaceable.
appearance.build: Broad and low, heavy with cold-stored fat across the whole frame, with limbs a little short and a core temperature a little low, so that from a distance he reads as unfinished.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly waxy, flushed only at the nose and the knuckles, the skin of a body that has spent most of its life at the cold end of its own range.
appearance.hair: Long, and the only head of hair on the ridge that is not cropped for wind: oiled flat against the skull while he stands the hours, and plastered down over the ears before a storm.
appearance.eyes: Small, dark and slow, with a pupil that stays narrow in bright snow and a habit of shutting completely when he is reading a scent off the wind.
appearance.palette: Oiled hide brown, storm grey, and one bleached white on the pass chain. The value range is broad and cold, and the only warmth in the frame is the sheltered orange of the pass lantern, which is the only warm thing on the ridge.
appearance.attire: Layered hides and oilskins cut short at the waist so he can lie down still wearing them, a heavy chain at the belt, and a stuffed hood that folds flat behind his neck in a single movement.
appearance.marks: Frost-split heels, an old burn along one forearm where a chain has jumped its pin, and a beard that frosted white inside the first hour of every rotation.
appearance.bearing: Low, wide and unhurried, standing with his back to whatever weather is coming and his face to whatever is arriving, because he can tell them apart a quarter-mile out and cannot always say how.

canon.role_in_story: The ridge's standing contradiction. He is the best long-haul body in the record, the only one that treats a winter as an asset, and a sworn Keeper of the pass, which makes him responsible for every hour of the crossing and forbidden to refuse a traveller. The sixfold's congregations cannot forecast their own duty, because the pass is scheduled by the Tidemark rather than by its holder and the swift flock owns the worst hours of it, so a household staffs the watch by conscription rather than by wage. He is therefore sworn to stand, through the season he is built to sleep in, on the only border in the setting where a border that shuts has to be shut by hand.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a change of watch on the pass chain, standing entirely still with his eyes shut and his hood folded flat behind his neck, while a traveller he had not yet seen came up the last of the slope; he had decided by scent alone which of two men was crossing, and refused no traveller either way.
canon.lore: A longwinter packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, and that one decision puts the flank vessels out of reach: they require two warm gradients held simultaneously, and this body has one, briefly, in summer. Ordinal seventeen is the first gate that needs both, so the species reaches far and never stays there, and the record is careful to say this is not a shortage of anything. His qi accumulates rather than circulates, so his breakthroughs are late and very rarely fail, and his soul sits deep enough to be difficult to read and harder still to damage. Everything a body needs for a haul across country, and nothing whatever for a fight. The Sixfold keeps one pass and the pass is not open, it is scheduled: temporal law is written on this tier, so the crossing runs against the Tidemark, and the swift flock crosses in the season the gale is worst, occupying the only usable hours for part of every year. The flock is a co-holder of the pass that cannot be reasoned with, and it caps how absolute any gate there can ever be. Because the holder cannot choose that schedule and cannot forecast it, the ridge cannot pay a garrison, since a garrison would be wages for hours a bird decides. The answer the frame arrived at was conscription by household: one adult per rotation, unpaid, unrecorded and unexemptable. A person who cannot stand is exempted. He has never been exempted, on the grounds that a body built to hibernate for eleven weeks is the most reliable body on the mountain, and every household that has argued otherwise has lost to arithmetic. So the winter he is made to spend is spent standing at a chain in the worst hours of the flock's season, in a frame that is warm, slow and large: a target that cannot be woken quickly, posted at precisely the place where being slow to wake is the whole of the risk. He smells the weather a quarter-mile out and sorts a stranger by it before he sees them, and the oath forbids him turning any of them away, so the most reliable nose on the ridge is bound to lift the chain for anything that walks up the slope.
history: Born into a ridge household on the far side of the pass, timed into the thaw like the rest of them, and put on the chain at fourteen because the rotation takes one adult and he was the only adult in the house.
Was exempted twice for a frost-split heel and returned to the chain both times, because the exemption is for people who cannot stand and he was being exempted for standing badly.

Finished his first full hibernation and came up out of it harder than he went in, which is the discovery the ridge's whole arithmetic rests on and the reason nobody has seriously proposed leaving him off the chain.
Cleared the seventeenth gate inside three weeks of one summer and lost it again before the year turned, which is the species' condition written as a single man's season.
Began marking the flock's hours on the chain posts in his own hand so that the next keeper would know which watch was going to be the bad one, and found that nobody had ever recorded them at all.

personality.summary: Unhurried to the point of immovability and stubbornly warm about everyone who is neither weather nor animal. He treats a duty as a debt he intends to pay in full and a forecast as something nobody on this ridge is entitled to, and he has been proved right about the second often enough that nobody believes him about the first.
traits: goes still while a decision is being made and speaks afterwards, at length
sorts a stranger by scent before he looks and never mentions having done it
counts out loud when he is angry, in fives, and stops on the fifth
treats an exemption as an insult offered to a body he is proud of
answers any question about the future with what the last eleven winters did
mannerisms: shuts his eyes completely to read the wind, which looks like sleep and is not
folds the hood flat behind his neck in one movement before any weather at all
plants both boots and lets the frame sway rather than shifting his weight
wipes the frost off a chain pin with his bare hand and looks at his palm afterwards
offers food first and the reason for it afterwards, in that order, every time
motivations: wants the flock's hours recorded in something that outlives a post
wants to finish a winter on the chain rather than in a sack below the pass
wants his households' rotation written down instead of conscripted
wants one full eleven weeks under the treeline and has never once been granted it
wants to be exempted from something, on any ground, so that the refusal can be entered in a book
flaws: has never been refused anything, and so has no practice at being refused
tells people what the last eleven winters did and treats it as a prediction
cannot move quickly enough to matter and has arranged an entire life that does not require it
takes the worst watch every year and has stopped explaining why, which reads as stubbornness
personality.voice: Slow, warm and concrete. He talks in weathers, distances and appetites, and describes a plan as something that happens if you are still alive in the morning. To a clerk he sounds slow; to a household that has spent a winter beside him on the chain he sounds like the only reliable person in the valley.
taboos: will not leave the chain while a traveller is still on the slope
will not accept a forecast he could have smelled for himself
will not take an exemption signed for pain instead of for standing
will not wake a hibernating body for anything short of a fire
refuses the title of keeper, on the grounds that the office cannot be ordained and neither can he

relationships.note: A cold-climate body that survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle, packing a winter as fat rather than as qi, which is excellent for a haul and useless for a fight. A warm decade is a catastrophe for this species and a long winter is simply the method, so the eleven weeks he is never granted are the whole of his training and the whole of his complaint.

A border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so somebody must stand on it every hour of every year by rotation, and its god is the flock that arrives. He is one rotation of that, which is the only form the congregation can take.

To stand the hours, to open and close the pass on the flock's schedule and not on any other, and to refuse no traveller. The second clause is the one his body exists for and the first is the one his physiology resists, and the third is the one that costs the most when he is half awake at the turn of a bad watch.

The pass is scheduled by the Tidemark rather than by its holder, and the swift flock owns the worst hours of it. The prize is the right to issue the wind, and the frame's answer was conscription, which means the hours nobody wants are staffed by somebody who cannot refuse them and cannot leave.

The flock crosses in the season the gale is worst, occupying the only usable hours of the only crossing for part of the year, which makes it a co-holder that cannot be reasoned with. He posts the hours it owns, marks them on the chain posts in his own hand, and has never once been given a season in which it does not.

Temporal law is written on this tier, so the crossing runs to a schedule and can be surveyed and closed and reopened, which is the setting's first choke point. The cost of having a schedule is that the schedule belongs to nobody: a law that moved on a cycle is the only reason the pass can be timed at all, and the only reason its keeper cannot time himself.

reference_stats.summary: Outlasts weather, distance and bad food better than any body on the mountain, and cannot be hurried, which makes him a campaign in a straight line and useless as anything else. The question is never whether he can arrive but whether anybody else can be made to arrive when he does.
strengths: Carries a load over cold open ground for weeks on a body that has to eat enormously and can digest frozen food better than anything alive
Stores a season as mass, so a missed ration costs him days rather than capacity
Reads scent at a quarter-mile in wind that blinds everyone else, which makes him early warning rather than combat
Queues rather than circulates, so a breakthrough that begins on him almost never fails on him
weaknesses: The seventeenth gate needs two warm gradients at once and he has one for a few weeks a year, so every gain is temporary and the losing is routine
In torpor he is large, warm and immobile and cannot be woken quickly, which is the worst possible state to be posted in the worst hours of the flock's season
Cannot be relieved of a duty he does not want, because the exemption is for people who cannot stand and he demonstrably can
Everything he knows is seasonal, and the pass keeps time on a cycle that is not his
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not choose ground and does not manoeuvre. He stands somewhere, is enormous and slow and warm, and lets an opponent exhaust itself against a body that will still be there, which is a legitimate tactic exactly twice in a lifetime. Anyone who can put the weather between them, or who can wake a flock at the wrong hour, has taken the fight out of his hands, and the setting's own record names the flock as a co-holder for that reason.
notes: No stat line models a body whose strongest asset is the state in which it must not be found, and that absence is the design.

The only population on the mountain that could be legitimately exempted from the watch is the one population the watch exists because of, which is an arithmetic argument nobody on the ridge has ever won.

art.palette_notes: Oiled hide brown and storm grey carry the figure with a wide cold value range, one bleached white on the chain, and the sheltered orange of the pass lantern as the only warm event. Ink line is broad and soft at the edges where the cold would blur it and tight at the chain and the hood, and the light is a lantern held at waist height because that is the only light on the pass and he works in it.

identity.realm: No ordinal is quoted and none should be. Eleventh is not blocked for this body, it is meaningless, and the difference is the whole of her. Her conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian: qi enters in the gut lumen, leaves into the marrow, and is never still. The reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold. She clears the gate set and every yin-organ gate on throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel to hold in. So she is not below a ceiling. She is outside the only kind of scale the ceiling is written in, and there is no rung to be caught short on.

appearance.presentation: A long, soft, entirely non-human outline. She reads as someone assembled out of a person by removing the parts that hold a shape: no muscle anywhere, a long apron of loose grey cloth hung from the shoulder line because a body this soft needs carrying, and a mouth that is set slightly open as though the sense were still arriving. Three fingered hands, held low and apart, always with the palms turned out.
appearance.age: Indeterminate, and she says so. Her soul is unusually old for the age her face presents and she has never found a reliable way to say which of the two she is. She was read as thirty when a village read her at seventeen and she has stopped correcting anybody.
appearance.build: Mostly tube. A marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle, an expandable gut and a very long small intestine, so her trunk reads as heavy and low and her limbs read as sightlines rather than as limbs. She is broader sitting than standing.
appearance.complexion: Grey and waxy, cool to look at and unpleasantly damp at the joints. Salt-white around the mouth and throat where the tissue is thinnest, and a faint dark seam along the spine where the marrow sits nearest the surface.
appearance.hair: Sparse, fine and colourless, grown in a short uneven fringe at the nape and shaved close elsewhere so that nothing is caught in the work. It is kept short because a long fall of it holds the smell of the last four readings.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set, matte and still, with a fixed wet shine that never blinks in rhythm with anything. They do not focus fast. They go to a room in the order the room died in, not in the order the room is arranged.
appearance.palette: Bone, ash and a cold wet slate, with one band of undyed homespun at the shoulder and a single dark iron ring at one finger. Nothing saturated anywhere in the frame.
appearance.attire: Fully covered: a high collar, long sleeves gathered at the wrist, covered shoulders, and a long apron of the same undyed cloth, doubled at the front because it is the part that is washed most often and the part that is washed least.
appearance.marks: A dark seam along the spine where the marrow lies nearest the surface, and a ring of finer grey at the throat. Both are the colony's own tissue and neither is a scar, though people ask about them.
appearance.bearing: Stooped and unhurried, with the shoulders carried low as though the room's ceiling were the only thing worth respecting. She enters other people's grief the way water enters a low place: without asking, and all the way to the edges.

canon.role_in_story: Every office in this setting is constituted by one clause: a reading counts if it is independent, and a reading is independent if no party with a stake in the answer holds the record it reads. Three auditors may sit at once. A gate is opened by one seated party and confirmed by a second who did not hold it. That clause is the only reason any of it is worth anything, and it runs on a single assumption underneath: that the second party is available. Garn Siltrow is the case that shows the assumption was never written down. Her species reads a body that has stopped far better than any living cultivator reads their own interior, so she is the most accurate reader of a death in this world, and a death is the only subject she has ever been able to read well. She is therefore the one body whose testimony is unconditionally competent and permanently inadmissible, because a body that has stopped cannot be the confirming second party to anything. She has been called in eleven times to settle a question about a person. She has answered eleven times. Every answer was correct and not one has ever been filed, because filing it would mean a dead person certified the living. That is the whole of her standing and it is not a personality or a refusal: the office of second party in this setting is the only thing her species can do, and the only thing her species cannot be appointed to, and both halves of that are authored rather than unfortunate. She is unaffiliated because the one seat her body fits is occupied by the patient.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in a mortuary doorway with her apron already off and folded over one arm, standing with her back to the wall and her open hands at her sides, waiting for somebody to come out of the room and tell her the answer she had already given the body.
canon.lore:
She reads the dead. That is the whole of what she is for, and it is worth being exact about how good she is at it, because the setting has no other instrument of that quality and one that everybody refuses on principle. Given time with a body she can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped, and she can do it without an instrument at all: she tastes qi the way a commonborn tastes salt, so a body's residue is a flavour with a figure in it. Nobody in this setting is better at this. That is not an estimate; it is the reason a mortuary college keeps a sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the reason the cases accumulate.

And then there is the appointment problem, which nobody wrote down. A reading counts if it is independent, and it is independent if no party with a stake holds the record it reads. This is why three auditors sit and a fourth is refused on capacity rather than a pair, and it is why a breakthrough at the field is certified by somebody the frame classes as an outsider, so that no practitioner of a tier judges his own kind. Every one of those arrangements assumes the second party is available. It is the mechanism, and the mechanism runs on a body being somewhere, alive and interested, able to be asked.

She is not. Not for this. A body that has stopped cannot confirm anything. It has no stake, which sounds like an advantage until you notice that having no stake is exactly what disqualifies a witness: a party with no stake is a party with nothing to lose, and the setting's entire verification architecture is built on somebody having something to lose. So her readings are the most reliable in the world and there is no office in this world that may file one. She is the standing proof that the independence clause has a second condition nobody stated, which is that the second party has to be alive.

She has been in and out of eleven rooms on the strength of it. She has answered eleven times, every answer correct, and not one has been filed. What happens instead is the thing that happens when a correct reading cannot be filed: it goes back into the person who heard it, and it comes out of them in pieces over years, in a form that is no longer a reading and is never again going to be one. She has watched this happen to herself eleven times, and she has never once been asked whether she would rather have answered wrong and kept it.

She has settled on a practice, and the practice is the whole of her character. She gives the answer in the room, aloud, to whoever is standing in it, and then she asks for the piece of it the person can carry. Not the figure. The figure is the part that gets her asked in. She asks for the sentence about the person: what the body was doing in its last hour, what it had been avoiding, which of its own habits survived to the end. That part is admissible. It carries no gate and no realm and no reading, and it can be said out loud in front of a family without anybody in the room becoming a party to anything. It is the only part of her work that survives the room, and she has never seen it done anywhere else, and she has never explained where she found it.

What she wants is narrow and she is clear-eyed about it. She wants the college to state once, in a line, that a body which has stopped cannot hold a record, so that the eleven readings she gave are on the record as refusals rather than as silences. She is not asking to be seated. She has established that she cannot be seated and she has stopped wanting it, which is a slower thing to give up than a person expects. What she wants is for the door in that building to have a notice on it naming the reason, because right now every office in this setting looks at a sealed case and sees a difficulty, and the difficulty is a woman with three fingers and a good nose.

What she will not do is stop reading. She has been offered three times to learn a technique that would let her take a living body's measure, which is the one thing that would make her admissible, and she has refused three times, and the reason she gives is the correct one and she knows it is unpersuasive: a living body is somebody's, and a dead one is nobody's, and she is not going to be the reason a living person gets read by a stranger with a good nose. She has been told this is a distinction without a difference. She agrees and has not changed her mind, and she is aware that the two of those facts is the sort of thing a person says when they have run out of reasons.
history: Read for the first time at eleven years old, in a leeward yard behind a house where something had been buried badly, and did not understand for two years that she had read a body rather than guessed at one.

Taken on by a mortuary college as a body that could be useful at a funeral, on the understanding that usefulness at a funeral meant carrying things, and discovered inside a season that what she could do was read.
First reading given aloud in a room with eleven people in it. It was correct. She has the note she wrote it on and no copy of anything filed anywhere.

Began the practice of asking each family for one sentence rather than a figure, after the fourth refusal, having worked out that the figure was the part that made her a party and the sentence was the part that did not.
Refused the three offers of a technique that would let her read the living, and has since declined to explain why to anybody who did not already know.
Asked, in writing, for the second condition on the independence clause to be printed. The request is filed. It has been neither answered nor refused, and she checks.

personality.summary: An unhurried, entirely unsentimental woman who has made a discipline out of the one thing her body permits and has accepted the cost of it with more patience than anybody finds comfortable to watch. She is not modest about what she can do. She is modest about what it is worth, and she has done the arithmetic on that twice and arrived at the same figure both times.
traits: Reads a room in the order it stopped rather than the order it is arranged.
Can be alone with a body for a day and will be, and does not find it difficult.
Has a standing refusal and has never softened it in conversation.
Keeps a written note of every reading she has ever given, in order, and has never been asked to produce the file.
Asks for a sentence rather than a figure and does it in the same breath as the reading, so nobody has to wait for permission.
mannerisms: Enters a room backwards, shoulders first, so the smell arrives before she does.
Keeps both palms turned out and away from her body at all times, as though apologising for the hands.
Speaks last in any exchange and answers at length when she does.
Wipes her mouth with the back of her wrist when a room has been open too long.
motivations: wants the second condition on the independence clause printed in one line at the mortuary college, so that eleven correct readings are refusals on the record rather than silences
wants one of the eleven questions she answered put to her again, years later, by somebody who wants to know whether she is still right
wants the sentence practice written down somewhere it can outlive her, because it is the only part of her work that has ever survived a room
wants to be asked to stop, once, by somebody entitled to ask, so that she can find out whether she would
flaws: Has organised her entire working life around a distinction she cannot demonstrate to anybody who does not already believe it.
Answers first and asks permission afterwards, in rooms where the answer is a person's whole afternoon.
Keeps the file. Eleven correct readings, in order, and cannot say what she intends to do with it.
Has twice refused an offer on grounds that were correct and unpersuasive, and knows the difference, and does not have a third argument.
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and precise, with a deadpan that reads as a joke and is never one. She describes what a body did in its last hour in the tone of somebody reading out a delivery note, and the flatness is not a defence; she has checked. She answers a question the whole way to the end of it and then stops, and the stopping is the only punctuation she uses.
taboos: will not read a living body, for any reason, including money
will not take a figure into a room with a family in it
will not let anybody else read her notes, and will not say why
will not be thanked for a reading, and deflects it every time

relationships.note: The conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen, leaves into the marrow, and is never still. Eleventh is not blocked for this body, it is meaningless: the reservoir gate asks for vessels that hold and there is none. She clears every other gate on throughput alone. Three-fingered hands built for opening rather than holding, and a body that is mostly tube.

Three auditors may sit and the fourth is refused on capacity, because an audit is only independent if no party with a stake holds the record it reads. The whole mechanism runs on a second party being available, and it was never written down that the second party has to be alive. She is the case that shows the omission: a body with no stake is a body with nothing to lose, and nothing to lose is exactly what disqualifies a witness.

relationships.kind: the office that keeps the sealed cases
relationships.note: At a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify. The cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body. She is what that produces, standing in its doorway, and the ambiguity is the college's standing revenue rather than its failure.

A fifty-year body whose fuel is its own furnace, which lost population at exactly the rate it could not stop and now holds the year's dead together as a declared group rather than keeping a growing store of the long-lived. It is exactly her attendance pattern, and she has never seen the parallel herself, and has stopped finding it interesting.

One sealed case per uncertifiable death, and no procedure anywhere in the setting for a certified death on a frame where life law is seated and spent. She could close more of these than anyone alive and every one she closes is a case that cannot be closed, because the answer comes from somebody who is dead.

A faith whose burial law opens the dead and recovers their usable ore to the forge, with the register recording how much. It exists because a rite that seals a body cannot also leave the material unreturned. She has been inside a sealed vault with the reading party and has walked out, and has never been asked to explain, and has never offered.

reference_stats.summary: Not a fighter and not mistaken for one. She wins by being the last person still willing to walk into a room nobody else will enter, and by knowing what she found there. Her whole capability is a reading taken from something that has stopped, which means she is strongest exactly where every other available option has been withdrawn and weakest the moment anybody is alive and moving.
strengths: Reads a stopped body better than any living cultivator reads their own interior.
Enters places the living will not, and is not troubled by what she finds.
Has an unbribable ear: she cannot be threatened by any method in the setting, because a threat requires something she can be compelled to accept and she is not attached to anything that can be taken.
Keeps a complete ordered record of her own work, which nobody else in her trade does.
weaknesses: A full gut is close to a total loss of function, and there is no warning.
Cannot read the living, by choice, and so is blind to anything still in motion.
Inadmissible in every room that matters, which means her best work has no standing.
Slow to focus and slow to start; the accuracy is real and the patience it costs is charged to whoever is waiting.
reference_stats.combat_read: Will not fight. The one thing she is good at happens after the last blow, which means in a fight she is a bystander with an inconvenient accuracy. Any opponent who keeps moving is simply out of her range, and she has never once pretended otherwise to somebody trying to kill her.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage above is paired with a cost that is in the record rather than invented here. The reading is unmatched and it only works on a body that has stopped, and the cost of taking it is the thing that makes the reading unusable: the second party is the patient. The dispassion is a temperament, and it is the temperament of a person who has decided the work is more important than her judgement of it, which is a position that can be wrong about a particular body. The refusal to read the living is hers, it is not the bible's, and nothing in this record says she is right to hold it. The load she carries in a settlement is a moral cost and not a magnitude: a full gut costs her function, and there is no gate behind it to reach for when it does.

identity.realm: Fourteenth, and the mechanism is her own feet. Ordinal 14 is the first gate requiring both heel vessels at once. Her wading frame is a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop, so the heel never takes a full load and qi never pools there. She walks fine. She cannot stand still, and the two heel vessels are the price of standing still. This one is a real wall and she has hit it, which is worth saying plainly because the honest kind of ceiling is the one you can describe accurately.

appearance.presentation: Long, folded and low, with the whole weight of the body carried forward on a tripod. She stands in a wide splayed three-point stance at all times, even in a doorway, and a reader unfamiliar with the species will read the stance as a peculiar way of posing. The tail-prop is used constantly and casually, braced against whatever is within reach.
appearance.age: Thirty-one, and she says it like a figure read off a gauge. Marshfolk age on the flood rather than the year and she has been counting thaws since she could walk.
appearance.build: Broad through a shallow pelvis and long-legged, with almost no calf to speak of and a deep prehensile tail-prop that carries a good share of her weight when she stops. The frame is built for silt and it is visible in the shape: everything low, nothing upright.
appearance.complexion: Cool, damp and faintly translucent at the throat and the inner arm, with a slick darkening across the shoulders that is the sun's work rather than a pigment. Skin that dries visibly within an hour of leaving the water, which she manages with grease.
appearance.hair: Long, black, rope-thick and kept in a single heavy braid laid over one shoulder, re-wetted and re-braided every morning without exception. Loose at the temples and beginning to thin at the crown in the way the species does.
appearance.eyes: Large and dark and set wide on a broad face, with the lower lid heavy. They track vibration before they track anything else; she will look at a floor and then at the thing that was moving on the floor two rooms away.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, reed green and black braid, with one band of undyed felt at the throat and a single pale bone toggle at the hip.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and cut for wet: a high collar, long sleeves bound tight at the wrist, covered shoulders, and a layered skirt of oiled felt over oilskin that goes to the knee and sheds everything. Bare feet in a salt-and-bitter country, deliberately.
appearance.marks: The splayed toes and the fused-looking webbing between the second and third, and a pale band at the hairline where a braid has been wet for thirty-one years.
appearance.bearing: Low, wide and permanently braced, in a way that makes a doorway feel narrow. She cannot stand still and the whole of her bearing is a permanent act of balance, which she has had so long that it reads as composure and is closer to arithmetic.

canon.role_in_story: Every institution in this setting enrolls by descent. A household wants a name and a line. A school wants a lineage. An office wants a register entry and something behind it that can be traced, and the trace has always ended at two people who stood somewhere and were recorded. Nissa Underbark is the case that shows what happens when the trace leads somewhere else. Her species fertilises externally and needs standing water, so conception happens where the body is: on a mat of woven reed laid on a particular stretch of standing water, at a particular point in the flood. There were two parents. They are named in her family's account. There is also a bed. Every office she has ever approached has wanted the descent and been given the descent, and every one of them has then asked the same second question -- whose mat, which water, what season -- because a line that terminates in a place rather than in a pair cannot be walked back, and a line that cannot be walked back cannot be checked against anything. She is unaffiliated because her species' only claim to an origin is a stretch of water that moves, and every office in this setting enrolls by counting back to two people.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched on the sill below a pass with her coat already off and her hands in the water, having answered a question about the water level that nobody had thought to ask her, and then waiting, without any sign of impatience, for somebody to come and ask her a second one.
canon.lore:
She was conceived in water and everybody knows it. That is not a scandal and not a secret; it is how her species works, and the mat she was set in is a family heirloom that has been kept dry for thirty-one years on her account. Her mother still keeps it. The problem is not the fact of it. The problem is what an office has to do with it.

An office enrolls by descent. The register line wants a household and a name, and behind the name it wants a pair, and behind the pair it wants somewhere they stood. It is a tracing procedure and it is the same procedure in every office in this setting, from a mortuary college to a crossing ledger to a school on the plains. Walk a person back far enough and you arrive at two people who were somewhere, and then the somewhere has to agree.

Hers walks back to a bed. A mat of woven reed, laid on standing water, on the flood. The flood is the only fact about her conception that has a location, and it is a location that has since moved, because a floodplain margin moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement standing on it. Her family can say whose mat. Her family cannot say where the mat was, in any way that anybody can check, and the reason they cannot is not that the record was lost. It is that the thing the record would point at is not in the same place twice.

So she has been refused nine times, and the refusals are all correct, and she has learned to do the second half of the conversation herself. She offers the mat before she is asked. She offers the parents, the thaws, the hatching. She has learned that the question is not whether she has a family and it is not whether the family can vouch. The question is always the same third question -- whose mat, which water -- and the answer is always a stretch of water, and the office always does the same thing with it, which is to put it down and look at her. She describes the flattening afterwards as being asked to produce a person.

What she does instead is the crossing, and she is very good at it. The frame that cannot stand still is the frame that can cross silt that will not hold a foot, and there is one place on this ground where the useful work is repeatedly standing somewhere nobody else can stand. She is at a sill below a pass, where the gauge has to be read from a position the water keeps changing, and she can hold the reading because she feels a vibration through standing water a long way before she can see where it came from. She reads the water. She does not sign it, because a reading signed by the body standing in it is not a reading, it is a presence, and she has been made to understand that distinction the slow way and has not forgiven it and does not mention it.

The thing she has not done is decide what she is owed. She is the cheapest body at that crossing and the only one that can reach the places the gauge has to be reached, and the arrangement has run for six seasons on that arithmetic. She has never asked to be signed rather than merely read. She has asked for one thing, four times: that her figure be entered as a second reading rather than as an error, because that is the difference between a measurement and a complaint, and because a person entered as an error is a person the office has a figure about rather than a figure from. It has been refused four times and she has kept asking, and the reason she has kept asking is that the alternative is being an error herself.

She wants to be enrolled somewhere, and she has begun to think about what that would cost. Not the refusal. The refusal is arithmetic and she has done it. The cost is this: every office she could join would be joining a family, and every family is a claim on where somebody came from, and the one fact she has that nobody in her family has is that she came from somewhere that is now somewhere else. She has started saying, only to herself and only in the last two seasons, that she may be the only person alive who can be enrolled on a map rather than in a book. She has not decided whether that is a solution and she has not told anybody.
history: Set as an egg on a woven reed mat during the spring flood, and hatched when the water returned, which is the only birth her species has and the reason her family dates her by the thaw rather than the year.
Refused admission to a school at nine, on a question about her mat that she answered correctly and that could not be checked.
Began crossing at the sill below the pass at fifteen, because her feet hold where others do not, and has crossed there for six seasons.
Asked for the first time, at nineteen, to have her figure entered as a second reading rather than as an error, and was refused politely and in writing.
Learned to open every enrollment conversation with the mat before she is asked, after the fourth refusal, having worked out that the question is never the first one.
Stopped signing nothing and started keeping her own count of the water at the sill, and has begun to think of herself as a line on a map rather than a name in a book.

personality.summary: An enormous, slow, watchful woman with a very dry humour and a memory for exactly what she was asked that she has decided to stop forgiving without ever raising her voice. She is warm in company, unbothered by being cold, and completely unyielding on the one procedural point she has taken.
traits: Offers the difficult fact before anybody asks for it, every time, as a matter of ordinary courtesy.
Can hold a position in moving water that other bodies cannot hold at all, and thinks about this less often than she used to.
Takes an institution's arithmetic seriously before she takes its refusal personally.
Counts things nobody asked her to count and has never once been caught doing it.
mannerisms: Never stands with both feet evenly weighted; the tail-prop is always somewhere braced.
Leans her head to hear a vibration, in the middle of a conversation, and comes back to it without apology.
Wipes her hands on her skirt before she touches anything that belongs to somebody else, every time, and has never once been asked to.
Sits rather than stands when a room offers her a chair, and takes it with visible relief.
motivations: wants her figure at the sill entered as a second reading rather than as an error, because that is the difference between a measurement and a complaint
wants the crossing sorted in her own name rather than through a house that owns the season of it
wants somebody to tell her plainly whether a person can be enrolled on a map, because she has begun to believe it is possible and has nobody to ask
wants the water at the sill kept in a record she holds, and has not asked for this because asking would put her name on a document
flaws: Pre-emptively supplies her own disqualifying fact as a courtesy, and has never noticed that the courtesy is the disqualification.
Has priced herself for six seasons by what other bodies cannot do and has not noticed that the price is not hers to set.
Refuses to sign a figure she is entirely confident of, on a principle she has never had to defend out loud.
Keeps her own count of the water and has not offered it once.
personality.voice: Slow, level and warm, with a long unhurried rhythm that makes her sound half-a-beat behind everybody in the room. She answers a question completely and then adds the part she was not asked for. The humour is dry, arrives late, and is never explained afterwards.
taboos: will not sign a figure taken by her own body, at any rate or under any pressure
will not let her mat be described as a household record
will not accept an entry made on somebody else's reading of her
will not stand still for a portrait

relationships.kind: what she is, and why she has no descent
relationships.note: Fertilisation is external and needs standing water, so conception happens where the body is: eggs laid in a mat of woven reed, carried under the brood pouch through the dry season, hatched when the water returns. A three-point stance over splayed toes and a tail-prop never loads the heel, which is why ordinal fourteen is out of reach. She walks fine. She cannot stand still.

relationships.kind: the ground that moves out from under the claim
relationships.note: Floodplain margin: reed beds, seasonal marsh, delta edge, and the only ground in the setting that is water half the time and land the other. The bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement standing on it. Her origin is a point on it that is not there any more, which is why a line traced back to two people has to end in a place nobody can visit.

The Watch reads the crossing and renews the mark. The useful service at that crossing is re-finding the run rather than maintaining it, which is a measurement of distance, and distance requires a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have. She is the only rostered body that can reach the places the gauge has to be reached, and the only one who does not sign what she reads.

relationships.kind: the procedure that keeps failing on her
relationships.note: Distance is not conserved on ground that seats no spatial law, so no two surveys of the same ground agree, and every claim is settled by leaving a marker standing rather than by counting how far away it is. The protocol is sound. It is written for a body standing on a bank, and she is a body standing in the water it is measuring, so the second reading she is asked for looks to the office like a disagreement rather than a corroboration.

relationships.kind: the practice she grew up beside
relationships.note: Shore notice is how people on moving ground tell each other what the water did. It is not written, it is repeated, and it is the only record of a floodplain that has ever been reliable. She learned her whole trade inside it, which is why she reads a vibration through standing water before she sees its source and why she has never needed anybody to teach her to listen to a floor.

relationships.kind: the standing argument she is inside
relationships.note: The run moves its bed and the gauge does not move with it, so the figure at the sill has been disputed for four seasons. She is the body whose readings the argument is about and the only one who has never entered the dispute, because entering it would require signing, and she will not sign a figure her own body was standing in.

reference_stats.summary: A body that cannot be in the wrong place, which in a setting where the useful labour is repeatedly standing somewhere difficult is not a limitation but the only qualification that matters. She reads water by vibration, she is almost impossible to hurry and almost impossible to corner, and she has not once converted either fact into anything she could own.
strengths: Holds ground in moving silt that will not hold a foot at all.
Feels a vibration through standing water a great way before she can see its source.
Cannot be flanked, cornered or surprised from above, because being surprised requires noticing and she notices through the ground.
Cold-proof and slow to tire, and does not need to sleep in a way that leaves her helpless on the bank.
weaknesses: Structurally cannot stand still, so she cannot hold a station, a guard post or anything that asks a body to stay put.
Skin desiccates fast out of water, so long dry seasons cost her mobility before they cost anyone else anything.
One gate short at the heels, permanently, and she has hit that wall and knows its exact shape.
Refuses to sign, which makes her figure inadmissible in every office she works for and she has been told so four times in writing.
reference_stats.combat_read: Very difficult to fight and impossible to corner, in a way that has nothing to do with force: she is where the footing is and the footing is a decision. What she cannot do is hold ground, so any fight that requires her to stay anywhere is a fight she leaves, and she has made no attempt to disguise that.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with a cost that is in the record rather than invented. The frame that cannot stand still is exactly the frame that crosses silt nothing else crosses, and the same fact is why she cannot hold a station; one anatomical fact, two consequences, and the setting has not traded one for the other. The refusal to sign is hers and is not the bible's, and this record does not claim it is correct: it is an ethical position with a professional cost, which is the pairing the program asks for rather than a stat to be tuned. Nothing here is a magnitude and nothing here should be read as one.

No cast shadow; a soft contact edge under the splayed feet only, since she never stands flat. Ink contours heavy along the outer silhouette and doubled at the tail-prop where it braces; wash laid in flat blocks with dry-brush edges, oilskin painted last and opaque over everything.
