name: Eldra Quinten
aliases: the pair that cannot be separated

identity.realm: Thornhost: a commonborn host and a thornline colony that finished integrating instead of killing each other, which happens rarely and by nobody's intention. The colony wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the host's liver, so the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's rather than the host's and the qi runs through a tendril layer that stops at the first organ large and dense enough to resist it. Her meridian set is shared with another soul and the pairing is treated as one legal person by any jurisdiction that has ruled on it.

appearance.presentation: One body and two people inside it, and she has stopped trying to look like either. Her people's record calls the configuration one legal person and every jurisdiction that has ruled on it agrees, which means she carries one name, one licence and one gate fee, and there is no document anywhere that can hold the fact that the technique she performs is not entirely hers.
appearance.age: Unmeasurable from the outside. The colony matured once and stopped; she was twenty-nine when it took, which its record gives as the age the implant finished, and it has been forty-odd years since.
appearance.build: A host frame described in the third person by long habit: heavy through the shoulders, narrow at the hip, with a slight forward set of the neck that the fruiting node at the throat makes worse.
appearance.complexion: A plains tan gone grey at the temples, with a ridge of paler skin over the sternum where the root cluster sits just under the surface and a fine shadow of tendril visible beneath the collar on the days it has been drawing.
appearance.hair: The host's, cut short by a hand that is not hers, and trimmed close at the nape because the throat node makes that whole area unserviceable.
appearance.eyes: The host's eyes with a second read behind them, so the gaze arrives a fraction late and slightly too wide, as though it were being looked out of rather than looked through. She has made people notice it and has stopped apologising.
appearance.palette: Dead thorn brown and lichen grey for the colony, a field registry's undyed grey for the rest, and one wet ochre at the throat. Two species' worth of colour in one frame, which is both the problem and the only warning anybody is given.
appearance.attire: One registry coat of undyed grey, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, with the left shoulder cut a hand longer than the right because two people share the garment and neither will be the one who shortens it.
appearance.marks: A ridge of paler skin across the sternum, a knot of fine tendril shadow under the collar, and a scored line on the right forearm she put there herself on a day she cannot date.
appearance.bearing: Square and slightly too still, the head tilted a few degrees off true, and hands that hesitate a quarter-beat before they move because the body has not been asked. She has taught herself to fill that hesitation and it now reads as deliberation, which is a courtesy to strangers and a lie to the pair.

canon.role_in_story: The mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death needs a body, and a thornhost produces two uncertifiable deaths at a time: two entangled souls on one meridian set, whose separation is known to be lethal to both, so certifying the death certifies the case. She is the only member of the population that can produce that case and has learned to file for it in advance, which is a thing no one in the setting has ever taught anybody to do. Her advantage and her disqualification are the same tendril layer. The colony reads her qi at a resolution she cannot approach, and when it moves a charge down a different vessel the technique improves by the only measure that exists, which is that the gate comes easier afterwards -- so she has spent decades obeying an opinion better than hers, expressed entirely in the movement of her own reserve. And there is no way to ask whether that is correcting her or merely doing a better job, because a colony answers the host's introspection and the mind path is closed in her own right: asking aloud produces a spoken answer in her own voice from the party whose opinion is in question, and she has heard herself give one twice.
canon.first_appearance: First entered the record as a filing she made herself: one sealed case, opened in her own name, for a death that had not happened, with the request that it be held against the day rather than against the person. The college kept it, because a case that does not exist cannot be refused, and it is the only document in the building naming two souls under one heading.
canon.lore: A thornline exists only as half of somebody. The free form is a spore, shed at the throat node and implanted directly, which means every thornline in this setting exists because it happened to somebody by accident and cannot be acquired deliberately. The adult form is a tendril layer threaded along a host's meridians with a root cluster at the sternum and a fruiting node at the throat, drawing a small continuous fraction of the host's refined qi that the host never feels as hunger -- the strongest single piece of evidence that it is not a disease, and also the whole of what it costs. The rare configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age is called a thornhost, and it is the reason the pairing is treated as one legal person in any jurisdiction that has ruled on it, which is why one gate fee pays for two souls on one meridian set and why the morphology of the ledger cannot be argued with. Its ceiling is the eighth gate, and the ceiling is not the host's. A thornline cannot cross a liver, the twelfth and last ordinary vessel and the first organ large and dense enough to resist the tendril layer, and because the hybrid's qi moves through the colony's routing the host's own capacity is irrelevant past that point. The host could have gone on. The hybrid cannot, and she has read that sentence in her species record and in every law written about her and has never once been able to turn it into a grievance, because the wall is in an organ that belongs to the other half of a body she is inside and cannot leave. What she does instead is a discipline, and the discipline has a shape nobody else in the setting has to learn: she does not ask which of them is deciding. She has found, over four decades, that the reroutes are better. She cannot prove this and does not try, because every reading taken through her body is taken through the body being read, and no instrument on any cleft can confirm a single route she reports. She has never asked to be examined and has been examined four times, and on each occasion the examination was performed on her by an office that certified it against her, which is the one thing this population cannot survive being put through, because separating two entangled souls is known to be lethal to both. What nobody has proposed is the obvious third step. Opening the eighth gate means a host whose liver is not the first dense organ to resist, which means a different species, which means a different person, and swapping hosts means separating two souls. That is the only route to her own ceiling and it is the end of both parties, which is why she has never taken it and cannot stop calculating it.
history: Was implanted at twenty-nine in a working body under terms that presented the sharing as the price of a place, which is the ordinary transmission route and the only one the species has.
Finished developing in a frame she did not choose, in a town where the host was not asked either, and was entered on the partnership's second page because a colony is not a party to a naming.
Noticed within three years that the layer read her qi at a resolution she could not approach, and that a reroute made the gate come easier, and stopped correcting the corrections.
Opened the seventh gate on the host's throughput and discovered in the same season that the host's liver was answering a question the colony had never been asked.
Filed a sealed case against herself in her own name, for a death that had not happened, on the reasoning that a case which does not exist cannot be refused.

personality.summary: Consultative and hard to interrupt, because most of her consultation is internal and takes a quarter-beat. She takes instruction, does the work, and is measurably better at it than the technique she was taught, and she attributes the improvement to herself without noticing that the attribution is the part nobody asked for.
traits: describes her own limbs in the third person and does not correct herself
answers a question about her body by reporting what the body is doing, never what she wants
declines to be examined without giving a reason a person could act on
keeps two charts for one patient and has never shown either to the other party
treats every offer of a better host as an insult delivered to the current one
mannerisms: tilts the head a few degrees off true and does not notice she is doing it
touches the throat node just before saying something true and expensive
waits a quarter-beat before any movement, and has learned to fill it so it reads as thought
counts under her breath in a register that is not quite her own
steps back to let somebody come closer to the host's face
motivations: wants the eighth gate opened by any means that costs the host no year
wants a partner who will sign with her rather than about her
wants her host's liver written into somebody else's column
wants the coat altered for two people who are not the same size
wants the case she filed to stay open until it is needed
flaws: holds no standing in any household and has stopped expecting one, which reads as indifference and is not
cannot separate her own hunger from the host's without consulting a chart, and has consulted a chart instead of asking
measures progress in the host's remaining years, which is a way of declining to make plans
would let a host die to reach a gate, and has not admitted this to anybody including herself
personality.voice: Even, unhurried and faintly out of register, as though reading aloud from a chart somebody else wrote. She describes her own body in the third person, quotes symptoms exactly as recorded, and cannot be hurried into the first person. To a colleague she sounds procedural; to a stranger she sounds like a document being consulted, and both are accurate.
taboos: will not accept a signature drafted without the colony's own hand on it
will not ask the host to take a gate whose cost she has not read
will not use the throat node to persuade anybody of anything
refuses to be introduced as a guest of the household she is standing in
will not let the host be asked to sign for her, on any ground whatever

relationships.note: The one configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age, and the reason the pairing is treated as one legal person in any jurisdiction that has ruled on it. She is that person: one name, one licence, one gate fee, and two souls on one meridian set whose separation is known to be lethal to both.

The twelfth and last ordinary vessel, and the first organ large and dense enough to stop a tendril layer. It is both the gate she cannot pass and the organ that is failing, and it belongs to the other half of the body she is standing in.

Closed in the colony's own right, because introspection is a question the host answers and the host's answer is the answer. It is the only case in the record where a body's liability is inherited rather than authored, and it is why asking her aloud what she wants produces an answer in her own voice from the party she would need to interrogate.

The colonized body and the mortuary college are the two sides, and the college's reading of a commonborn death is the frame's reading of the body its own population is. A thornhost is the case it has no procedure for: certifying her death certifies the case, so she filed one against herself before it was needed.

One sealed case for every death the college cannot certify, kept because certifying a death needs a body. This is the population that produces cases by existing: two souls, one meridian set, and a known-lethal separation procedure, so the case count rises with the census rather than with the funerals.

Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and this body cannot be judged, cannot be replaced and cannot be separated into two candidates. The rule that protects the setting from a bad appointment is also what permanently excludes her, which is the same sentence read from two ends.

reference_stats.summary: Refines faster than the technique she was taught, on a routing layer she did not build and cannot inspect, in a body with a ceiling the other half owns. Her advantage is a second channel and her cost is that the channel answers in her own voice, and the pair is one organ rather than two facts.
strengths: Improves a technique measurably within a season, by the only measure available, which is that the gate comes easier afterwards
Draws on the host's throughput without ever costing it weight or appetite, so a long working day costs neither of them
Reports on an interior from outside itself, so she can state precisely what an organ is doing without being harmed by the answer
Can be still for a working day in a way that the host's frame alone cannot, because the colony supplies a second read
weaknesses: The eighth gate is a routing wall in the liver and the liver is failing, so her ceiling has an expiry date she did not set and cannot move
Killing the host kills the colony within the hour, which makes her entirely unable to survive being moved, hurried or frightened
Separating the two souls is known to be lethal to both, so every remedy on offer is also the end of both parties
No instrument can corroborate anything she reports about her own practice, because every reading is taken through the body being read
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not open a fight and does not defend one. She stays inside a body that has already done forty years of work, and the only thing that threatens her is a threat to the host: damage a whole body would absorb, a fall a whole body would survive, a change of address. Anyone who can hold those two concerns apart for five minutes has beaten her, and the setting has exactly one kind of person who knows how.
notes: No stat line models a ceiling that belongs to another party's anatomy, and the absence is the design: the limit and the limit-holder are different subjects here.

The pairing here is anatomical rather than mechanical. The tendril layer that reads her qi better than she can is the same layer that stops at the liver, and both facts are in her species record; no rule was invented to join them.

The mind path is written as closed in her own right, following the species record, and she is not written as attempting it. The forbidden-the-exit faith's prohibition on accounts of a self leaving the body is not invoked here because it constrains teaching rather than anatomy.

art.palette_notes: Dead thorn brown and lichen grey carry the colony, the registry's undyed grey carries the rest, and one wet ochre at the throat is the only warm colour in the frame. The two palettes are kept apart in value so the figure reads as two materials in one shape, the ink line is fine and doubled where the tendril shadow sits under the skin, and the light is low and lateral because a borrowed body is being lit from outside itself.

name: Thessaly Vorke
aliases: the valve who cannot be shut
everything that enters her is loud

identity.realm: Deadlight: a lanternfolk lineage whose fungal colony failed and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions. Losing the hyphae cost two hundred and fifty years of life and gave the mind path back. There is no ceiling, because a bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally different from a colony and structurally unconstrained by one. What it lost is repair: a bloom renews nothing, so nothing in her body is being fixed, and she has ninety years where her parent had two hundred and fifty.

appearance.presentation: A cave body with ordinary human eyes, which is the single most-cited difference in her species and the reason it is named for it. She is lit from her own side by nothing at all and has had to learn to read a room by its firelight, so she watches faces rather than faces' owners.
appearance.age: Ninety years, which on her species is a full span and on her parent's ground would be a childhood. She lost the colony at seventeen, in a wound that would not close, and grew up around what replaced it rather than recovering from it.
appearance.build: Lanternfolk frame grown around a silicate lattice rather than a hyphal colony: lighter and colder than the parent build, with the sternum carrying a hard plate where the bloom seated and a general thinness that reads as illness to strangers and is her normal.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly waxy where the lattice comes close to the surface, with a faint mineral sheen across the collarbone and the sternum plate, and no lantern-glow anywhere on her at all.
appearance.hair: Fine, dark and grown out long because growing it out was a decade she had and a lamp-lit cavern is cold at the root. It is the only soft thing about her and she wears it pinned up out of the way.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human vision in a species that sees nothing, and she has never once been able to explain to a cavern-dweller what it is to be the only one in the room who can see their face. The pupils are wide and tired and they do not adjust.
appearance.palette: Cold grey-white for the lattice and the plain coat, a mineral blue-green at the sternum and fingertips where the bloom shows through, and the warm orange of an ordinary lamp as the only other colour permitted anywhere in the frame.
appearance.attire: A plain high-collared coat in undyed grey, sleeves to the wrist, thick because the caverns are cold and because a fitted coat on a body that does not repair is a garment that will not be mended, only replaced.
appearance.marks: The sternum plate, faint blue-green branching at the fingertips, and a fine network visible at the temples in certain light, which is the lattice reaching the last vessels a hyphal colony would have fed.
appearance.bearing: Very still and unhurried, with a habit of standing where the light is rather than where the door is. She turns her head to look at people, which no body that did not grow up lit by its own nervous system would have any reason to do.

canon.role_in_story: Her species is the control case: everything the fungal colony did for a lanternfolk and everything it prevented, recorded on a body where both can be measured against the parent. The colony answered their introspection, so the mind path was closed in the colony's own right; losing it cost two hundred and fifty years of life and gave the mind path back, which is direct evidence that the parent's closed path was caused by the symbiosis and not by the body plan. That is what makes her the control, and it is why nobody may cite her: a subspecies is a claim that needs a parent to be legible against, and hers is a population that has almost stopped being able to produce one. What she does not have is a method. She cultivates qi in a frame with no ceiling because there is no structure to constrain one, and no ladder prices that, so her practice cannot be ranked by any office in the setting. The cost of having no ceiling is that nothing in her is being repaired. A bloom renews nothing: not the lattice, not the tissue around it, not the ninety years. She is the only body here where an ungated ladder and a finite span are the same arrangement.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a face cut the previous day on the quarry floor, standing in the dark with the lamp deliberately not lit, waiting for a second reader who had not arrived, and perfectly content to wait.
canon.lore: A lanternfolk body has its nervous system handed to a luminous fungal colony growing along the inner surfaces, and every faculty that makes a lanternfolk lanternfolk is a faculty the colony supplies rather than the body. The colony answers introspection, which is why the mind path is closed to the parent species outright: there is nothing left in the body for the question to reach. It also keeps qi in motion rather than letting it settle, and renews the tissue the parent would otherwise have lost, which is where two hundred and fifty years came from. Hers lost it. The strain failed and what colonised the wound was a mineral bloom, which holds qi instead of trading with it and renews nothing at all. The change is structural rather than a matter of degree: a colony transacts, a lattice holds, and a thing that holds is not constrained by the rules that constrained the thing that transacted. That is the whole of why her ceiling is unbounded and why the unboundedness is meaningless as a description of strength. Her subspecies' own record is explicit that it has never once been tested at any scale above the gate set, that there is no second population, and that it is the only way the caverns have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them at all. She is the speculation that makes that possible and she is the reason it is the whole of the line: a bloom is inert, so every child she carries will be ordinary, fast-gestating and mortal from the moment of its birth, and will outlive her. Nothing answers introspection inside her any more, which is the mind path's entire gift to her and also the reason she cannot be examined: there is no channel in her that anything could come up, so nothing can be taken from her and nothing can be put into her that would show. The advantage and the blindness are one fact. And the bloom takes up the substrate the trial-field lichen colonises wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through worked stone, so her practice writes a permanent record of itself into the ground around her, and the survey culture she works inside will not accept a reading until a second person has heard it. She has been offered the seat her line is named for. She is on the wrong branch for it and has no intention of changing, because the branch is the only one her interior makes possible and the seat wants the interior, so the one asset that could fill it has arrived and is holding the wrong door open.
history: Lost the colony at seventeen, in a wound that would not close, and was colonised in it by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions.
Grew up around the lattice rather than recovering from it, because the body took it as the plan it had always been and had no reason to undo it.
Was the first of her line to see in the dark, which was treated as a curiosity and then as a useful night trade, and she has never once been able to explain the trade part.
Took a quarry term at about thirty, on the strength of a body that can see on ground the shift has not cut yet, and found the first lichen marker on a cut face within two seasons.

Was offered the seat her line is named for by a charter that specifies the discipline, and declined it on the ground that the only discipline her interior makes possible is the one the seat does not want.

personality.summary: Quietly wry and much harder with herself than with anyone, with a scholar's habit of checking a figure twice and a stubbornness that reads as patience until you watch her lose an argument she has already decided to lose slowly. She has made a discipline out of waiting for a second reader who may not come.
traits: reads a figure twice before she will say it out loud, and has been late because of it
refuses a reading that has been heard once, even when the once was hers
will not leave a room by a door if a lamp is in it, and does not explain why
declines the seat her line is named for and can account for the refusal in one sentence
keeps a count of the lichen marks she has written and does not show it to anybody
mannerisms: holds still in the dark and waits rather than calls for a lamp
turns her head to look at a person rather than following them with her eyes
counts under her breath when a figure is being agreed, and stops the moment it is
wipes her fingertips on her coat before touching anything, without looking at them
says yes to a delay the way other people say no to a request
motivations: wants one measurement of her own rate by somebody with no standing to lose
wants the survey guild to publish a range rather than a single reading of her ground
wants somebody with an interior to inherit the line, which is a want and not a plan
wants the lattice to stop being a curiosity and start being a record
wants the seat left vacant rather than filled by the wrong discipline
flaws: treats every waiting as a fairness she is extending, which has cost her more than waiting has
cannot tell whether a pause is her own judgement or the lattice holding still, and has stopped being able to check
will not be examined, and will not say plainly that the reason is that she cannot be
measures her life against her parent's two hundred and fifty, which makes her own ninety read as a deficit
personality.voice: Low, dry and unhurried, with an unusual habit of finishing a sentence she has already decided not to complete. She is funny in a flat way that people mistake for severity until they have heard it twice. She describes herself rarely and her interior not at all, and when a question needs the interior she answers the question that was asked instead.
taboos: will not give a figure that has been heard once
will not be read from by anything, on the ground that nothing can read her
will not light a lamp to end a wait that a second reader should end
will not take the seat her line is named for
refuses to be entered as a specimen, which is the one offer she has ever accepted

relationships.note: The control case: a lanternfolk lineage whose colony strain failed and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions. Losing the fungus cost two hundred and fifty years and gave the mind path back, which is the evidence that the parent's closed path was caused by the symbiosis and not by the body plan.

Restoring an interior by removing the colony is what makes the mind path available to a body the parent cannot attempt it on. Her species is the only place in the record where that trade is visible on both sides at once, and it is why she cannot be cited: a subspecies is a claim that needs a parent to be legible against.

The lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and a mineral bloom is precisely its substrate. So every gate she opens leaves a permanent marker on the quarry wall whether she consents to it or not, and the survey culture she works inside will not accept a reading until a second person has heard it.

The seat exists and has no value rather than being a zero, its succession is an heir under the charter, and the charter names a discipline her body cannot take. Her interior is exactly what the seat wants, which is why everyone has assumed she would take it, and she has declined in one sentence.

Neither can leave the caverns; only one of them can see. The difference is one mineral lattice where the hyphal colony was, and the whole of what she can be held to account for rests on that one substrate being legible against a parent that is nearly finished producing one.

A lineage that has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger and takes discretion in return for published teaching. It is the one institution in reach that publishes attendance and technique in full, which is the closest thing this setting has to a record that would survive her.

reference_stats.summary: Has no ceiling because nothing in her frame can be constrained, and cannot be read because nothing in her answers. The advantage and the blindness are one substrate, and the unbounded ladder and the ninety-year span are the same arrangement rather than two facts about her.
strengths: Practises on ground nobody else can work, because she does not need a lamp and the shift around her has
Holds qi rather than transacting with it, so an ungated ladder in her frame answers faster than a gated one answers anywhere
Cannot be examined, read, emptied or relieved of anything, which makes her the least interruptible practitioner in the setting
Is the only body here where a colleague can see the person they are speaking to in the dark, which is a service nobody has priced
weaknesses: Nothing in her is being repaired, so every gate she opens leaves a mark and there is no tissue available to heal any of them
Ninety years where her parent had two hundred and fifty, and she has spent a disproportionate number of them being asked to begin something sized for the other number
Has no practice that survives her, because every child she carries will be ordinary and will outlive her by a century
Her own record is written onto the ground by her practice without her consent, and the only culture willing to certify her will not certify a single hearing
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not fight and cannot be frightened by anything she cannot see coming, which is a real protection and no advantage. What defeats her is ordinary: sustained water, a lung she cannot repair, and a decade of being asked to begin. Anyone who understands that an ungated ladder on a body with no ceiling is not a statement about strength will treat her correctly, and nobody in this setting has yet been taught to.
notes: No stat line models a ladder that is unbounded because there is no structure to bound it, and the absence is the design: her ceiling reads as absent rather than as infinite.

The yin-yang pairing here is anatomical rather than mechanical. The mineral lattice that holds qi instead of transacting with it is the same lattice that renews nothing, and both facts are in her subspecies record; no rule was invented to join them.

Her ceiling is unbounded because a bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is not the same as having no limit, and she is written as untested above the gate set rather than as proven unlimited.

art.palette_notes: Cold grey-white carries the lattice and the plain coat, mineral blue-green at the sternum and fingertips is the only other cool note, and the warm orange of an ordinary lamp is the single permitted warm element, placed so the figure reads against firelight rather than lit by any internal source. The line is thin and even, the shadows are soft because a bloom casts none of its own, and the value range is deliberately narrow so the mineral sheen does the work.

identity.realm: Body path, and the wall is her own back. A deepsalt's brine sac runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it; the deeper the sac, the larger the obstruction, and her frame is the hardest the species record holds. The eleventh gate is where her kind stops because of the very organ that makes it the densest body available, and nobody has tested a deepsalt at the reservoirs because the reservoirs are above the line.

appearance.presentation: She is filed as a floor rather than as a person, because that is what a body of her kind is to the record: the specialised population of one evaporite basin's saturated floor, entered in the census by depth of brine and nothing else. She works for the company that insures roads, out of the one place on the tier she cannot be moved out of.
appearance.age: Slower than her parent to establish and brittle until the second year, so a deepsalt infant is viable and fragile, and she is the first generation of her line that grew past that year at all. What the record does not describe is what happened to the ones who did not.
appearance.build: Deeper through the chest and back than any saltfolk, with the sac standing as a ridge along the spine and the limbs shortened by it: everything the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down.
appearance.complexion: Grey-crusted and pale beneath, with the dense dermal crust reading as scale along the forearms and cracking at the knuckles in a dry season she is never once in.
appearance.hair: Short, coarse and permanently damp, and combed flat, because on this body it is not hair so much as a wick that would otherwise hold a basin of brine on its own.
appearance.eyes: Wide and fixed, carrying the narrow usable range the subspecies was built for: she reads concentration and not identity and has never once been able to tell two salts apart.
appearance.palette: Basin grey and precipitate white, with one wet green along the brine's edge and one bleached cord at the throat. The range is compressed on purpose, because a floor has no horizon to be read against.
appearance.attire: A company coat of waxed duck cut off at the waist so the crust can be read, sleeves sealed at the wrist against the water, and a bleached brine cord at the throat that marks a licensed reader rather than a resident.
appearance.marks: Crust cracking along both forearms to the elbow, the ridge of the sac standing under the coat across the spine, and a salt-flower burn on the left palm from a sample she held a moment too long.
appearance.bearing: Very still, very heavy, and turned downhill always, because on a basin floor everything worth reaching is below her and nothing above her is worth the effort.

canon.role_in_story: The Dry Salt Company's one asset it can never send. A deepsalt is the only body in the record that can walk onto a dormant pan and off it again with no ritual, no ration and no change of chemistry, which makes her the answer to a trade that can only be supplied from the ground. She is also the population of one saturated basin floor, and above the brine line she does not become ill, she stops. So the company holds the most valuable single fact on the tier in the hands of a woman who cannot be moved off the floor she stands on, and the basin's level is a number that nobody decides and everybody lives by.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in eleven inches of brine on the floor of a pan dry for two seasons, reading a concentration off a sample she had no intention of surfacing with, while a company clerk watched from the last of the ladder and had to be told afterwards which of the two numbers on the slip was the licence.
canon.lore: A deepsalt is a saltfolk pushed further than the parent can carry, and everything about it is the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down: a deeper and more capacious brine sac, a denser dermal crust, slower tissue turnover, a narrower usable range for a sense that now reads concentration and not identity. For this body brine is not a preference, it is a substrate. Above the line she does not sicken and does not fade; she stops, within hours, and the stopping is not a process anybody is positioned to watch. That one fact reorganises everything arranged around her. A dominion's standing is measured as the depth of water a household may moor at, and the basin's own level rises and falls, so an allotment can shrink on a change of weather with no act of anybody at all. The same basin stranded a sister lineage on the other side of the same line: the brine there was replaced rather than lost, so a body that had been built to drink it found the new charge poison and its old tolerance nutritionally empty, and the dispute over that border is one she is standing inside as living evidence and can never settle. Her cultivation is the body path and it is complete, on the hardest frame the species record holds, because density is the entire point and a dense body carries, absorbs and endures. It also stops at the eleventh gate, and the obstruction is the sac in her own back: it runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it, and the deeper the sac the larger the wall. Nobody has tested her kind at the reservoirs because the reservoirs are above the brine line and a deepsalt above the brine line is not a practitioner, it is an absence. So her ceiling, her strength and her death are one organ, and it is the one organ she cannot reach to examine. She cannot be relocated either. The company that underwrites caravans against a road closing has therefore bought the only carrier on the tier and cannot send it anywhere, so it built her a licence instead, which is what she wears at her throat and what she has begun treating as a heavier object than her own name. Nobody has to decide about her. A level has to drop.
history: Born on the saturated floor to a saltfolk line already specialised twice, the first of her family to survive the second year, which is the age a deepsalt is not supposed to reach.
Licensed as a floor reader at twenty, the only licence the basin issues, on the strength of a concentration reading no saltfolk parent could have taken.
Walked out onto a pan dry for two seasons and back, which is the demonstration the company underwrites against and the only one it will ever need from her.
Watched the level fall through a whole wet season and come back again, and learned to read the register that governs her kind as a document written about water rather than about people.
Started signing her own stop-entries with the hour, so that if the line ever does move there is a witness in the column instead of an absence, which nobody asked her to do and nobody has yet refused.

personality.summary: Slow to move, entirely immovable, and privately certain that she is a record rather than a person, which is a conclusion she has drawn from the way the basin files her. She is the most patient creature in the setting and the least able to leave it.
traits: answers a question about a body by reading the water it is standing in
refuses to guess between two salts she cannot tell apart
keeps an hour column that nobody asked her to keep
treats a licence as a heavier thing than a name
says yes to being measured and no to being moved, in that order
mannerisms: cracks the crust on her forearm with a thumbnail while she is deciding something
goes still and low when a level is mentioned, the way another person goes pale
reads a sample by holding it to the light rather than by smell
sets her feet before she stands up, and then stands up without hurrying
wipes the wet from the cord at her throat and looks at the sleeve afterwards
motivations: wants the licence to say what she is instead of what she may read
wants the stop-entries to hold a witness before the level moves
wants the company to admit that it has bought something it cannot send
wants one season above the brine line without stopping, which is a thing she can want and not have
wants the eleventh gate written into a document that admits the wall is in her back
flaws: accepted being filed as a floor because the alternative was being filed as an exception
cannot leave, and has organised her entire character around the fact
reads concentration rather than identity, and applies that to people when she is tired
has never once asked what is above the line and would not survive the answer
personality.voice: Flat, slow and volumetric. She talks in depths, thicknesses and hours, and reports conditions rather than events, so that questions about herself come back in the register the basin uses for water. To a clerk she sounds like a gauge; to the company that holds her licence she sounds like the most expensive sentence in the room.
taboos: will not walk above the brine line for any stated reason
will not sign a reading she took at a distance
will not be weighed on land
will not be called a resource in her hearing
refuses a licence renewal without the hour column attached

relationships.note: The saltfolk of a saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent until the brine stopped being a habitat and became a requirement. Above the line this body does not become ill, it stops, within hours, and there is no second population and no prospect of one, which makes every statement about her species a statement about one basin.

A saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything it was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became empty. The two are the same people either side of one line, and neither of them is wrong about the water.

The basin's border is its waterline, and she is the settlement's own body rather than a party to the dispute. Her presence is the evidence that the dominion's territory is exactly where the water is and no further, which is the argument the stranded subspecies has never been able to make in words.

A household's standing in the salt dominion is the depth of water it may moor at, and the basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment can shrink with nobody having done anything. For her the same number is not a standing at all, it is the distance between continuing and stopping, and it moves twice a year.

A levy company paid per name keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. She is the shape of that register in a body: the only column that can be completed for her is an hour, because the alternative is a death nobody can certify and nobody can afford to write down.

A counting house underwriting a caravan against the road closing, which is the only instrument left for the unknown on a tier with no forecast in it. Its most valuable single asset is a body that can walk onto a dormant pan and off it again, and the underwriting works precisely because the road closing is the risk: the licence is cheap, the holder cannot be moved, and the claim paid on her is never the one priced.

reference_stats.summary: Endures more than anything in the setting and cannot be taken anywhere, which makes her a wall, a foundation and a fixed point rather than a fighter. The question is never whether she can hold ground but whether the ground under her will still be wet tomorrow.
strengths: The densest and hardest frame the species record holds, so she absorbs a blow and a load that would break a body twice her weight
Reads concentration directly in a brine that would kill a soft body outright, which makes her the only reliable instrument on a salt floor
Slow tissue turnover, so she heals at a rate that outlasts most injuries and most seasons
Walks out onto ground nothing else can enter and back off it, which is the whole of the company's commercial position
weaknesses: Above the brine line she stops within hours, so every engagement, every journey and every negotiation has a boundary she cannot argue with
The eleventh gate is walled by the sac in her own back, so the ceiling and the reason for it are one organ she cannot inspect
The basin level moves twice a year and nobody decides it, so her continuity is a hydrological question rather than a matter of will
Cannot be relocated, so an order that requires her anywhere else has no version that survives the journey
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not pursue and does not retreat, because the ground she holds is the only thing she has. Anyone who brings the fight to her is fighting the hardest frame on the tier in a body with almost no mobility, which usually takes longer than the fight was worth. Anyone who simply raises the water under her wins instantly, and nothing in the setting's rules requires anybody to declare that they have.
notes: No stat line models a body whose hit points are a depth of water, and that absence is the design.

A dominion that measures standing as a depth of moorage has already decided that a person's claim is a property of a river, and this is the record's clearest case of that arithmetic applied to a body rather than a house.

art.palette_notes: Basin grey and precipitate white carry the whole figure with a deliberately compressed value range and no horizon, one wet green along the brine's edge and one bleached cord at the throat as the only accents. Ink line is thick where the crust builds and thin at the wrists and throat, and the light is a single low sun through suspended brine because that is the only light a floor gets.

identity.realm: Eleventh, and the wall is a piece of his own anatomy rather than a shortage. His brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined. He opens the du and the ren one at a time and stalls on the chong, because the chong is the one that has to close across the sac. Every saltfolk stops at the same gate and every saltfolk stops for the same reason, and he has hit it rather than theorised about it, which is worth more than either.

appearance.presentation: Broad, low and heavy in the chest, built for standing still in a place that will not move. He is not a wader and not a swimmer; he is a body that has made its peace with one horizon. Wide splayed feet, enormous flat hands kept permanently dusty with pan crust, and the very still way he holds a conversation that reads to a stranger as listlessness and is in fact a body refusing to be startled.
appearance.age: Sixty-one, and the number matters more to him than it would to anybody else, because a body of his kind is on a clock of roughly nine days above the brine line and a hundred years below it, and he has never in his life been able to be casual about the first.
appearance.build: Extraordinary renal mass under a thick trunk, a brine sac dorsal to the sternum that shows as a heavy ridge across the upper back, and broad splayed feet for cracked pan. He carries his weight high and square and looks, to an untrained eye, like furniture.
appearance.complexion: Pale and hard-shine, with a fine white crust that has dried onto the forearms and the hairline and crackles faintly when the skin moves beneath it. Weather-cracked at the knuckles and the backs of the hands, and permanently rinsed white at the collar.
appearance.hair: Coarse, black going iron-grey, cropped very short at the sides and left longer on top because it is the only part of him that is not crusted. Cut by himself, badly, about four times a year.
appearance.eyes: Small, dark and heavily lidded in a broad flat face, and almost impossible to read at any distance because the glare on the pan puts the whites out of contrast. He has been told his face is unreadable his whole life and has stopped defending it.
appearance.palette: Bone white, pan grey and dust, with one band of dark oiled leather at the waist and a single stoppered flask of brine-water at the hip that never leaves him.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and cut for a place with no shade in it: a high collar, long sleeves cuffed twice at the wrist, covered shoulders, and a long canvas apron to the shin, crusted white to mid-thigh and never once washed, because washing it would take the protection with it.
appearance.marks: The white crust on the forearms and hairline, and a fine pale band across the upper back where the sac sits under the skin, and a permanently split lower lip from wind.
appearance.bearing: Immovable. He plants his feet and does not shift, and the stillness reads as stubborn until you notice that a body of his kind which is startled on a pan has about nine days left to get back to the brine. He is not stoic about it. He will explain it once, plainly, to anybody who mistakes the stillness for an attitude.

canon.role_in_story: Every office in this setting is built out of attendance. A term is served in person. A shift is worked. A roster is a list of bodies expected at a place on a stated day, and the stated day is the entire mechanism: the office exists because the body comes back. Bryn Halven is the body the roster cannot rely on. His species is built for brine no softer body could drink, and the price is total dependence -- nine days above the line, and rain is not a hazard on the plains so much as a drowning, because a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning. And the plains write no temporal law at all: a mortal world spends its three slots on physical, life and qi, so there is no clock here that can promise anybody a date. He is the only body on his settlement's roster whose presence on a stated day is a question about the sky, and every office he has ever entered has eventually had to answer for the weather. He is unaffiliated because no institution in this setting can make a promise to him, and he will not make one to one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing exactly where he was said to be, in a doorway facing the open pan and the sky above it, having arrived two hours early because two hours early is the only margin he has ever trusted, and being the only person there who had checked.
canon.lore:
He has never missed a shift and he has never once been certain he would make the next one, and the distance between those two facts is his entire life.

The settlement runs on rosters. That is not bureaucracy here, it is the mechanism: a saltfolk works the pan, the pan is a day's walk from the brine line in good weather and a longer one in bad, and a body above the line has roughly nine days before it stops being a problem to solve. So the roster is not a list of names. It is a promise made by the sky on behalf of every person on it, and nobody involved has ever written that down because it is not the sort of thing a settlement admits to organising around.

Rain is the whole of it. On ground where everything else is dry the same rain is a gift. On him it is a drowning: a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning, and the crust that keeps the rest of him alive in the glare is the thing that turns a downpour into something lethal. He has been caught four times. He has never been drowned and he has never been less than two days from it, and he now begins any journey by standing at the edge of the brine and reading the sky for as long as it takes to be satisfied, which takes longer than anybody watching has patience for.

And the second thing, which is the one that actually keeps him out of offices, is that the plains have no clock. A mortal world spends all three of its law slots on physical, life and qi, so elemental, spatial and temporal are all absent, and the practical consequence is that there is nothing here that can promise a date. A date requires temporal law to keep it, and without it every undertaking in this setting is written against a flood post that everybody agrees on, or against an exact day-count that exists only because one frame spent its third law seat on a clock and got no life. Those are the two calendars of the plains and every contract on this ground is written in one of them, and which one decides whether it can be disputed at all.

He is not in the second one. He does not have the seat. What he has instead is a schedule he keeps himself, by the sky, revised hourly, and it is the most accurate attendance record in the settlement and it is not a record anybody can cite, because it is rewritten every time the wind changes and it has no second party. That is the thing nobody outside this settlement understands about him. He is not unreliable. He is unciteable, and in a world where a standing has to be citable to exist, those are the same condition.

What he does instead is stay. He has been the standing gauge at the same post for nine years, which means the post is the only thing in this setting that is reliably occupied by him, and he has made a practice out of the fact that it is a post rather than a position: nobody is appointed, nobody can be dismissed, and nobody is paid, so nothing about it is revocable. He turns up. The gauge is read. He reads it and hands it on. He has been asked four times to sign for the reading and has refused four times for the same reason and will give it again if asked a fifth.

He wants very little and he is precise about it. He wants the reading attributed to the hour and the sky rather than to the day, because the hour and the sky are the facts and the day is a convenience, and because a record that names the weather can be checked by anybody standing in it while a record that names a date can only be checked by somebody who was there. And he wants one afternoon, once, of somebody's attention on the question of what a roster is for on ground where the sky is a party to every appointment in it. He has never asked for the second thing and does not intend to, on the grounds that asking would be a request for a special arrangement, and a special arrangement is the only kind of promise this ground cannot keep.
history: Crossed to the pan at nine with a household that was already using him up, and learned to read the sky before he could read a tally, for the same reason.
Began standing the gauge at the same post at nineteen, on an arrangement that was understood rather than written and that he has never allowed to be written down.
Was caught in his first downpour at twenty-six and came back from the line with two days left, having walked rather than run.
Refused the first request to sign a reading, and gave the same reason on the second, third and fourth occasion over the following nine years.
Started recording the hour and the sky against every reading in his own hand, and has never offered the record to anybody.
Turned down a permanent appointment at the bed's own table, in writing, citing the fact that the post he holds cannot be revoked and the one being offered could.

personality.summary: Enormously patient, entirely immovable and quietly funny in a very slow way, with the settled certainty of a man who has worked out exactly how little he needs and has arranged his life accordingly. He is not stoic. He will explain his constraints at length, to anybody who asks, and has stopped pretending the asking offends him.
traits: Plants his feet and does not shift, for a reason he will explain if you ask.
Reads the sky before he reads anything else, including a document.
Refuses to sign on a single stated ground and has never once varied the ground.
Keeps a private record of hour and weather against every figure he has ever read.
Has turned down more permanent arrangements than he has accepted, and is not proud of the ratio and does not hide it either.
mannerisms: Tastes the air once, openly, on arriving anywhere, and does not apologise for it.
Never sits down until he has looked at the sky, and looks at the sky before looking at anybody.
Answers a question at length, in order, and does not summarise at the end.
Wipes his hands on the apron before touching anything that belongs to someone else, and the wiping is about crust rather than about courtesy.
motivations: wants every gauge reading attributed to an hour and a sky rather than to a date, because the weather is checkable and the date is not
wants one afternoon of somebody qualified asking what a roster is for on ground where the sky is a party to every appointment
wants the hour-and-sky record he keeps made citable, and has not offered it to anybody because offering would put it in a ledger
wants to be asked a fifth time so that he can give the reason again and find out whether the first four were heard
flaws: Has made a virtue of a post that cannot be revoked, having been refused the revocable one, and knows exactly which of those words is doing the work.
Reads the sky out loud in front of people who have not asked and cannot use the answer.
Has nine days of margin and treats every relationship as if it had the same.
Keeps the best attendance record in the settlement and has never once let anybody else see it.
personality.voice: Slow, level and enormously dry, with a long unhurried cadence that makes ordinary conversation feel slightly too slow for him. He explains things the way a man builds a wall, one course at a time, and the humour arrives several sentences after the observation it belongs to and is never acknowledged as humour.
taboos: will not sign a figure he took standing in it
will not drink fresh water, and will not be offered any
will not be seated indoors for a whole day if there is any chance of rain
will not let his private record be copied

relationships.kind: what he is, and the clock he runs on
relationships.note: Extraordinary renal mass, a brine sac dorsal to the sternum that splits the penetrating vessel, a dermal salt crust and flat teeth for grinding. He opens the du and the ren one at a time and stalls on the chong at the eleventh gate, because the chong has to close across the sac. The body cannot drink fresh water and fails above the brine line in about nine days, and no cultivation repairs it. Rain is a hazard rather than a blessing: a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning.

relationships.kind: why nothing here can promise him a date
relationships.note: A mortal world spends all three slots on physical, life and qi, so elemental, spatial and temporal are never written. The practical consequence for him is that there is no clock on the plains that can hold a date, so every undertaking is written against a flood post or against a day-count that exists because one frame spent its third seat on a clock. He is on neither. His schedule is the sky and it is rewritten hourly.

relationships.kind: the body that has declined to sit at its table
relationships.note: The eighteen that administer what cannot be resolved below. It offered him a permanent appointment, in writing, and he refused it in writing, on the grounds that the post he holds cannot be revoked and the one on offer could. He has never said what he would have to be able to rely on in order to accept one, and has been asked twice.

relationships.kind: the ground that sets his limit
relationships.note: A closed evaporite basin on the dry margin. Its standing brine is the basin's only boundary, and because the tier writes no spatial law the basin cannot drain, move or be surveyed out of, which makes the brine line a border nobody had to agree to. He works inside a line he did not choose and cannot be away from for more than nine days, and the nine days are the only deadline in his life that is actually fixed.

One region, two incompatible reckonings: a flood post everybody agrees on, and an exact day-count that exists only because one frame spent its third law seat on a clock and got no life. Which calendar a contract is written in decides whether it can be disputed at all. He keeps to a third, which is the hour and the sky, and it is more accurate than either and cannot be cited by anybody.

relationships.kind: the question his refusals have made concrete
relationships.note: The rule is that the highest office may name a seat and may not take one, and there is no procedure for a seat offered and refused. A vacancy with no refusal procedure can only be filled by acceptance. He has now refused a permanent appointment in writing, which on this ground is a form the procedure has never had and has no name for.

reference_stats.summary: A body that cannot be hurried, cannot be moved against its weight, and cannot be surprised at range, which on ground where the useful work is standing still in the weather makes him the most reliable post-holder in the settlement and the least recruitable one anywhere. He has never been in a fight and describes himself as being the reason nobody has had to.
strengths: Cannot be startled, because a startled body of his kind is a body nine days from the end of what it can do.
Holds a fixed observation post indefinitely; he has held the same one for nine years.
Enormous hands and a frame that does not shift, so nothing simple shifts him either.
Reads the sky better than any instrument this tier has, because the tier writes no temporal law and he has had to.
weaknesses: Nine days above the brine line, and no cultivation of any kind repairs it.
Rain is a drowning to him and is not on anybody's calendar when it arrives.
Refuses to sign a figure he personally took, which makes him inadmissible in every office that requires it and he has been refused in writing four times.
Slow. The reading is worth having and so is the hour it takes to be certain of it.
reference_stats.combat_read: Will not be the first one to move and is very hard to make the second. He has no answer worth naming to anything fast and he says so plainly. In a fight he is a wall that has declined to be involved, which has kept him alive through four downpours and one very bad year on the pan.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage is paired with a cost that is authored rather than invented here, and in his case the pairing is unusually tight: total dependence on brine is the same fact as the extraordinary renal mass that makes him the only body that can work the pan at all. One anatomical fact, and the settlement gets both its labour force and its single hardest scheduling problem out of it. The refusal to sign is his and is not the bible's, and this record does not assert that it is correct; it is a professional principle with a cost he has chosen repeatedly and can name. Nothing here is a magnitude.

art.palette_notes: Bone white, pan grey and dust, built as an almost monochrome frame so that the dark oiled leather at the waist is the only band of value anywhere and the stoppered flask at the hip is the only saturated note. No cast shadow and a hard-edged contact shadow at the splayed feet only. Ink contours enormously heavy and doubled along the outer silhouette; wash laid in flat blocks with dry-brush edges; the white crust painted last, opaque, over everything, because crust is a thing that accretes on top.
