identity.realm: No ordinal is quoted and none can be. The mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally a different thing from a colony and is constrained by nothing a gate could ask about, and her own species record states that there is no ceiling without offering a gate at the end of it. What she gained is the mind path and what she lost is three quarters of her life, and both halves of that sentence are about the same substitution. She is not standing below a ceiling. She is the body in the deep ground on which the ceiling question does not arise, which is a different situation and not a better one.

appearance.presentation: A lanternfolk body that has gone cold: the same broad-shouldered, slightly stooped frame as the species she came from, but where a lanternfolk wears a glow like weather, she wears nothing at all, and the eye keeps checking her for it. She reads as a lantern that has gone out and been brought inside.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, and she is the youngest thing her age in the caverns and it is on her face in a way it is on nobody else's. A lanternfolk of a hundred and eighty is a child. A deadlight of fifty-eight is most of a life.
appearance.build: Lighter and colder than the parent: a silicate lattice where the hyphal colony was, so the frame is thinner through the shoulders and the limbs read as slightly too long for the body carrying them. The body grew around what replaced the fungus rather than recovering, and it shows in the way she carries herself -- all four limbs used, none of them braced.
appearance.complexion: Chalk-pale and faintly translucent, with the network of the lattice visible as a faint blue-grey tracery at the temples, the inner arm and the hollow of the throat. It does not warm. It does not flush. It has never done either.
appearance.hair: Fine, colourless and brittle, grown long and kept simply tied, because the parent grows it fine and colourless too and cutting it is the one part of the resemblance she has kept deliberately. It breaks rather than bends when it is moved.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human eyes in an extraordinary face: the only part of her that her subspecies did not cost anything to acquire. They see in the dark, which is the single most-cited difference in the record and the reason the subspecies is named for it, and the seeing is not a glow and is not warm and gives nothing back.
appearance.palette: Chalk, cold grey and the dull blue of the lattice tracery, with one band of undyed felt at the throat and a single bone-grey clasp at the shoulder. Nothing in the frame reflects light that did not come from a lamp.
appearance.attire: Fully covered, cut to her species' plan and heavier than a cavern body needs: high collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, a long felted over-layer with a worked shoulder clasp. She wears it in a cave system that is never dry and never warm, and she has never once felt it was too much.
appearance.marks: The lattice tracery at the temples, inner arm and throat, and a pale band at the wrist where her sleeve sits, which is the mark the parent's fungus would have worn if she had one.
appearance.bearing: Upright and unhurried in a place whose whole population stoops toward the ground, and she carries herself in the dark with the composure of the only person down there who can see, which is a composure nothing in the caverns has earned and she has not been able to put down since she was nine.

canon.role_in_story: The deep ground is a civilisation built on a body that does not decay. A lanternfolk colony renews neural tissue faster than a human frame does, so age stops mattering down there and a person is young for two hundred and fifty years; every office in the caverns measures a tenure in that clock, and every appointment, every succession and every argument about who is due what assumes the person in the chair outlives the argument. Vesa Colderby is the body that broke the assumption. Her lineage lost the colony and grew a mineral bloom in the wound instead, which gave back the mind path -- the mind path her parent has closed -- and took away a hundred and sixty years, because a bloom renews nothing and so nothing in her is being repaired. She is the only deadlight in the deep ground and she is the only body there that ages at the rate the surface does. Every tenure written in the caverns is longer than she will live, so she is unaffiliated because the deepest settlement in this setting enrols by counting out somebody else's remaining centuries, and she has not got any.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at a nursery junction in the dark with the lamp deliberately not lit, waiting for somebody to come along a passage she had already watched them take, and having walked them past three junctions without telling any of them where she was going.
canon.lore:
There is one settlement in this setting where nobody grows old, and she is the only person in it who does.

The caverns are lit by the population. That is not decoration: a lanternfolk's light is a waste product of a symbiosis nobody chose, it is emitted rather than received, and it is the only reason the deep caves have an economy at all. Everything down there is keyed to it -- the shifts, the pairing chambers, the nursery junctions, the whole enormous arrangement by which a colony is matched to a child inside a year or the colony rejects the child and takes the body with it. A lanternfolk does not age because the colony renews her neural tissue faster than a human frame does. Age simply stops being the thing that happens to her, and two hundred and fifty years reads as a young adult. The whole civilisation is built on that arithmetic and has never had to check it.

She has the mind path. Nobody else in the caverns has the mind path, because the colony answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. Hers was taken by the same hand that took her centuries: the colony died, a mineral bloom colonised the wound, and everything the colony did for her it did not do to her. There is nothing in her interior now. She can find out what she is. She has been the only person in the deep ground who could, and it turns out that is not a privilege when the settlement measures you by how many years you have left to spend.

So here is the arithmetic nobody checks. A bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is why her species has no ceiling and no gate to fail -- and a bloom renews nothing. Nothing in her body is being repaired. She is the only thing down there that is dying on the schedule the surface uses, and every office, every pairing and every expectation in the deep ground is written on a clock she does not run on. A household expects sixty years of a marriage. An office expects a successor. A nursery expects a matcher to still be walking in thirty years. She is the one body for whom all of those are the same length, and it is ninety, and she is fifty-eight.

She has been offered things. Twice she has been offered a place, and the first refusal was because she had not worked out the arithmetic and the second was because she had. She is not a person who is temperamentally outside anything. She is the control case standing in the only body in the record on which the whole arrangement can be measured from both sides at once -- everything the colony did for its parent and everything it prevented, legible on one frame -- and the settlement has known that for three generations and has argued over her instead of examining her.

What she has instead is the sight. That is the part of the trade nobody planned. She sees in the dark, ordinarily, with human eyes and no glow and no warmth given back, and it is the single most-cited difference between her and her parent and the reason her subspecies is named for it. It is also, in a civilisation that has spent two hundred and fifty years getting by without it, worth nothing. The caverns have no post for it. They have a matcher, a drafter, a nursery keeper and a hundred and forty other trades, and not one of them is the woman who can see the whole of a passage in the dark.

She wants two things and has arranged them in order. She wants the terminations written down as terminations -- every office, every pairing, every apprenticeship that assumes a lanternfolk span -- so that the ones that will outlast her are known to have been counted rather than assumed. And she wants somebody to be shown to her, once, on a measured morning and evening, so that the difference between her rate and the parent's stops being a thing the settlement believes about itself. She has asked for the second one twice. Both times she was told that a body which repairs nothing cannot be relied on for a long measurement, which is true, and which is also, she has pointed out and will point out again, a statement about reliability made to the only body anybody has for measuring it with.
history: Lost the colony in her ninth year to a strain failure, and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom that survived the same conditions her parent could not.
Learned in that same year that she could see in the dark, which nobody in the caverns had a use for and which she has therefore had to justify annually ever since.
Found the caverns' first term written in a lanternfolk span and counted what was left of her own, and did not sleep well and has repeated the arithmetic several times since.
Refused her first offered place, before she had the figures, on the grounds that she did not yet understand the offer.
Refused the second, in writing, having worked out that the offer's own terms assumed a remaining span she does not have.
Began walking parties through the dark junctions without a lamp, which is now so usual that nobody remarks on it and which she has been asked to justify twice and has not.

personality.summary: Very upright, very dry and entirely unillusioned about herself, with the specific humour of a woman who has read her own subspecies record carefully and finds the record funny. She is not bitter. She is early, in a way she has made useful, and the usefulness costs her every posting the caverns have ever had.
traits: Sees in the dark and has never once made a virtue of it out loud.
Can give you the remaining life of any lanternfolk-shaped body by eye, and has estimated her own.
Refused two placements in writing and has kept both letters.
Talks to her own subspecies record as though it were a colleague's report and frequently more reliable.
Will not be looked after, and has an entirely reasonable case and gives it at length.
mannerisms: Walks the dark passages with the lamp unlit and her hand flat on the wall, and is the only person down there who does not need the lamp at all.
Counts things aloud under her breath when she is working and does not notice.
Sits down in the middle of a conversation when she is tired, immediately, with no apology and no explanation.
Asks a question, waits the whole way to the end of it, and does not fill the pause.
motivations: wants every cavern appointment that assumes a lanternfolk span written down as assuming one, so the ones that will outlast her are counted rather than presumed
wants to be shown to herself once on a measured morning and evening, so the difference between her rate and the parent's stops being a belief
wants one office in the caverns to have a term that fits a ninety-year life, and will accept a short one
wants to be asked why she walks the junctions unlit and told that it is useful, because she has walked them unlit for thirty years and nobody has said so
flaws: Has organised her whole working life around the fact that she is dying and does not appear to have noticed that this is the same thing as organising around being tired.
Refuses placements on arithmetic that is correct, which has twice been read as arithmetic.
Has let thirty years of useful work go unnamed because the naming would have needed an office.
Counts her own span on a schedule and has not told anybody the schedule.
personality.voice: Level, precise and dry in a way that lands about two seconds late, with a deliberately ordinary delivery of things that are not ordinary. She uses the subspecies record's own vocabulary -- control case, span, transacting -- in the manner of somebody quoting a colleague, and she does not explain any of it twice.
taboos: will not have the light in her described as something she lacks
will not accept a term written in a span that assumes a colony
will not be carried anywhere, by anybody
will not be called a control case by somebody who has not read the record

relationships.kind: what she is, and both halves of the cost
relationships.note: A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice where the hyphal colony was: lighter, colder and entirely inert. The bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally different from a colony and structurally unconstrained by it, so her species' record states no ceiling without offering a gate at the end. What the subspecies gained is the mind path. What it lost is three quarters of its life, because a bloom renews nothing and nothing in this body is being repaired.

relationships.kind: descent, and the clock she does not run on
relationships.note: The colony renews neural tissue faster than a human body does, so age stops mattering and a lanternfolk of a hundred and eighty is young. That is why the deep caves have an economy at all -- their light is the only light down there -- and it is why every office, pairing and succession in the cavern system is written on a two-hundred-and-fifty-year clock. She is the one body in it that is not.

relationships.kind: the settlement that measures her wrong
relationships.note: Lightless karst and lava tube under the Spirit Peaks: saturated air, no daylight at any depth. It is the only ground in the setting where a body that lost its eyes first and a body that only inherited sight can both live, and the reason the two populations were never compared until the mineral replaced the fungus in one of them. She is that comparison, standing in it, on the side of it that ages.

relationships.kind: the dispute she is the whole of
relationships.note: What the colony did for its parent and what it prevented, disputed on a body where both can be measured against the parent species at once. She is the control case and has been argued over rather than examined for three generations, and the examination would require somebody to be shown to her on a measured morning and an evening, which she has asked for twice.

relationships.kind: the culture whose arithmetic she actually shares
relationships.note: A fifty-year body whose fuel is its own furnace, which lost population at exactly the rate it could not stop and now holds the year's dead together as a declared group instead of keeping a growing store of the long-lived. It is the only population in the setting whose life expectancy resembles hers, and it has never occurred to anyone on either side to say so, and she has decided not to be the one who says it.

relationships.kind: the argument she is evidence for and has never been used in
relationships.note: A heresy disputed over whether a test site exists, on a plain where the mind path is a body with the mind path open. She is the one piece of evidence in the setting that could settle it and she has been argued over rather than examined, which is the same sentence as the colony dispute with the subjects swapped.

reference_stats.summary: The only body in the deep ground that can see in the dark, which the deep ground has no post for, and the only one there that ages at the surface rate, which is the reason every post there is written wrong for her. She has no combat capability of any kind and is not a fighter, and the one thing she is genuinely good at is turning up in a passage nobody else can find.
strengths: Sees the whole of a dark passage, which the rest of her species cannot do and cannot learn to do.
The only unmediated interior in the deep ground: nothing answers introspection for her, so she can find out what she is.
No ceiling and no gate to fail, because a bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it.
Unlit passages, unaccompanied, at a time of day when nothing else down there is moving.
weaknesses: Nothing in her body is being repaired, so ninety years is the whole of what she has and she is fifty-eight.
Fragile, and more so with every year, in a settlement where the standard of toughness is a two-hundred-and-fifty-year body.
Cannot leave the caves, for exactly the reason her parent cannot.
Refused two placements in writing, on arithmetic that was correct, and is therefore unplaced by her own act.
reference_stats.combat_read: Will not fight and would be poor at it, in a place where the ordinary answer to a threat is that somebody else is older than the threat. What she can do is be somewhere nobody else in the cavern system can reach at all, in the dark, which has twice been the whole of a rescue and once the whole of an escape.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage is paired with a cost that is authored rather than invented here, and in her case the pairing is one anatomical substitution read from both sides: losing the colony gave her the mind path and took a hundred and sixty years. Nothing about that trade is a balance knob -- it is the subspecies, stated once. The two refusals are hers and are not the bible's, and this record does not assert they were right; she has recomputed the arithmetic each time and got the same figure, which is a fact about her and not a defence. Nothing here is a magnitude.

art.palette_notes: Chalk, cold grey and a dull lattice blue, built so that the frame contains no light source anywhere in it -- no glow, no bloom, nothing that reads as emitted, which is the single hardest thing to draw and the whole visual statement of a body defined by what it no longer does. One band of undyed felt at the throat and a bone-grey shoulder clasp are the only value breaks. No cast shadow and a soft contact edge at the feet only. Ink contours heavy and doubled; wash in flat blocks with dry-brush edges; the lattice tracery painted last, translucent, over everything.

identity.realm: Body path, and the ceiling is the parasite's rather than the host's. His qi moves through an integrated tendril layer instead of the host's own channels, and that layer has no passage through the liver, so ordinal eight is a wall in an organ he does not have. The host could have gone on. He could not, and he is the only practitioner alive who knows the ninth gate's price exactly, because he watched a host pay it.

appearance.presentation: He is presented as one person and audited as two, and he has made the distance between those two things his profession. The Cairn Field licenses no humanoid to attempt a breakthrough, so the reading must be taken by an outsider, and he is the only candidate in the record who is an outsider twice over: a host body and a colony, in one frame.
appearance.age: Old by the standard that counts and young by the standard that pays. A thornhost is the one configuration in which both halves reach old age, so he has had more time to prepare than anybody else at the Field and less time in which to spend it.
appearance.build: A host's frame with a thickening across the shoulders where the root cluster sits, and a neck that carries the fruiting node high enough to be read across a room.
appearance.complexion: Unremarkable at six feet and unmistakable at two: the skin over the sternum is faintly paler than the rest, and the throat carries a knot of fine tendril shadow under the surface that moves when he swallows.
appearance.hair: Cut close and grey at the sides, cut differently by two different people on two different days, which is the most reliable evidence anyone at the Field has that he shares a barber.
appearance.eyes: The host's eyes, and behind them a second read that arrives a fraction earlier than his own gaze does, so that he appears to be looking at somebody slightly past whoever he is speaking to.
appearance.palette: Oxide red and ash for the colony, bone white for the office, and one green-black at the throat. The white is the office and the red is the parasite, and he wears both inside one frame deliberately, so that nobody at the Field is ever in doubt about which law is reading them.
appearance.attire: A Reckoning Seat reading robe of bone white over a red underlayer, high-collared and closed to the wrist, with a gauge ring and a stick of sealing chalk at the belt, because a reader who certifies carries the instrument that certifies.
appearance.marks: The pale ridge across the sternum, tendril shadow at the throat, a fillet of red cord at the left wrist worn by every holder of the post, and a long healed seam along one forearm from a host he did not leave in time.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried and slightly turned, so the nearer shoulder faces the Field rather than the applicant and the throat and the sternum are both visible at once, which is what a reader is required to be.

canon.role_in_story: The Cairn Field's certifying reader, and the reason the office can function at all. The Field licenses no humanoid to attempt a breakthrough, so the reading has to be taken by something the frame considers an outsider, and a thornhost is the only such candidate in the record, being a host body and a colony at once; his rulings are therefore unappealable on grounds of species in a way no other verdict on the tier is. He knows the price of every gate on the plains better than anyone alive and cannot pay one of them himself, because his ceiling is the parasite's routing and not the host's capacity. What he sells is access. What he owns is the only ledger of what that access costs, kept in a register of deaths nobody has been able to certify.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the Field taking a reading off an applicant with both palms flat on that applicant's frame and his eyes shut, and when the applicant asked who had taken it he gave his own name and his partner's in the same breath without pausing, which was the first time anyone on that field had heard a ruling signed twice.
canon.lore: A thornhost is the single configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age: the tendril layer fully integrated, a root cluster at the sternum and a quiet node at the throat, neither half anatomically dominant, the boundary between them visible only under instrumentation. It is treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, which is convenient, and it is also the reason nothing can be done to him. His qi moves through the colony's layer rather than through the host's own channels, and the layer has no passage through the liver, so his ceiling is the eighth gate. That ceiling is the parasite's and not the host's, and the record is unusually plain that this is not a shortage of anything: qi is abundant, the host pays for it steadily and loses no weight, and the wall is purely routing. The host could have gone on. He could not. That single asymmetry is his profession. The Cairn Field holds every mortal-band breakthrough from the first realm to the ninth on the one tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one, so a body there cannot be judged by anything of its own kind and the reading has to be taken by an outsider; a thornhost is an outsider twice over, which makes his verdicts the only ones on the plains that cannot be set aside because the judge was one of the judged. The post is paid out of gate fees, and gate fees are the only tax the tier can actually collect, which makes him, in effect, the collection mechanism with a body. He has therefore read more ascensions than anyone alive and reached none himself. He knows the ninth gate's exact price because he watched a host pay it, and he has never been able to act on that knowledge since. Every host who leaves him leaves two souls on one meridian set and one document, and the mortuary college keeps a sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death requires a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body. His ledger is a case file: the largest accumulation of unopened coffins in the setting, every one of them his. Taking a second body is, in the plainest analogy available, a second seal, which is the one act a temple's own forge may not perform and the setting's only prohibition written with no mechanism behind it at all.
history: Was the first integrated pair taken to the Field after a host's family consented to a reading, and certified a first gate in a body that was not his own and could not be questioned about it.
Was granted the reader's post after an incumbent's ruling was set aside for species, which was the first time in a century that the office had gone vacant for that reason.
Started a bound register of every host who left him with the hour recorded against each, which remains the only document in the setting that names his own replacements.
Was offered a host whose liver was not the first dense organ to resist, and refused, and has never explained the refusal to the applicant who paid for the offer.
Began signing each verdict with his own name and his partner's, in that order, so that a clerk reading the roll can never tell which half of the pair decided.

personality.summary: Serene, exact and entirely incurious about his own ascent, because a reader who wants nothing from an office can be trusted to read it honestly, and he knows that better than anybody. He is the kindest certifying reader alive and the reason a set of coffins has never been opened.
traits: signs with two names in a fixed order and has never once varied it
asks an applicant what they expect the gate to cost before he tells them what it costs
will not certify a reading taken by anybody standing behind him
keeps a register nobody has ever asked to see
answers a question about himself by naming the host it was actually about
mannerisms: reads a frame with both palms flat and his eyes shut, in complete silence
wipes the sealing chalk on his thumb before a ruling and never after one
turns the nearer shoulder toward the Field rather than toward the applicant
says his partner's name in the same breath as his own, without hesitation
presses the flat of his hand on a case file's cover before he stands
motivations: wants every verdict in the roll attributable to a half rather than to the pair
wants the sealed cases opened and the register read, and knows both refusals are his to make
wants one gate past the eighth, and has understood for years what that costs and whose
wants the office to publish what a certification is worth rather than what it fetches
wants to be replaced, and has trained nobody capable of holding the post
flaws: has never refused a fee and takes the gate tax from applicants he has just read
sorts applicants by their capacity to pay the ninth gate and does not always say so
has replaced hosts in order to keep reading, and records the hour without ever recording a reason
cannot be examined twice, which is the only thing keeping him out of a case file of his own
personality.voice: Low, measured and unhurried. He speaks in the register of an office rather than a person, states conditions before opinions, and answers with two names where one was asked for. To an applicant he is the most reassuring man on the tier; to a physician he is a case file that answers questions.
taboos: will not certify a reading he did not take with his own hands
will not sign a single name
will not open a case file where the Field can see it
will not accept a host whose liver he has not been told about
refuses payment before the reading rather than after it, on a principle he has never explained

relationships.note: The one configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age, and the reason the pair is treated as a single legal person. Neither half is anatomically dominant, the boundary is visible only under instrumentation, and the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's rather than the host's, which is the whole of what makes him a certifying officer and not a practitioner.

The twelfth and last ordinary vessel, the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, and the first organ large and dense enough to stop an integrated tendril layer. He is walled at the eighth gate by an organ that belongs to the other half of his legal person, which is why the host could have gone on and he could not.

The mortal office that certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of gate fees, existing because the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind and the reading must be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. He is the only body on record that qualifies twice over, which makes the office's entire legitimacy one person's continued existence.

A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body while the frames keep producing the record without the body. Every host who leaves him produces exactly such a case, which makes him the largest single author of unopened coffins in the setting.

No socket may be opened once sealed and reforging one is the one act a temple's own forge may not perform, because a second seal is how the Iron Grief happened. He has no socket and opens one regardless, which is why this prohibition is the setting's only one written without a mechanism to enforce it.

A mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and a famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present, so the prize is which reading of a life is the record and it cannot be split. He has read every life at the Field as the frame said, and has kept a private register of the other reading, and the two have never been added up.

reference_stats.summary: Does not fight so much as adjudicate, and wins the way an office wins: everybody present is waiting for him to say the number. The question is never whether his verdict will hold but whether the applicant can pay for the gate he is about to be cleared into.
strengths: His rulings cannot be set aside for species, so in a dispute his word is the mechanism that ends it
Reads a frame faster and more accurately than anyone on the tier, because the second channel gives him a live account of the qi he is being asked about
The colony's durability carries the host through injuries that would end an ordinary body, and he has the reserve of a body that has been maintained for decades
Holds the only complete register of what a breakthrough costs at every rung from the first to the ninth
weaknesses: Walled at the eighth gate by an organ that is not his, so he has more authority than attainment and every applicant knows it
Killing the host kills him within the hour, so his invulnerability is entirely borrowed and he cannot be moved off a post he cannot defend from another direction
Cannot be examined twice, which means a hostile physician gets one look at him and he gets no second opinion on anything
Every host he replaces adds a sealed case to a register he personally maintains and personally refuses to open
reference_stats.combat_read: He declines. He reads an opponent's frame out loud in front of whoever is watching, which turns a private disagreement into a public certification, and a public certification on the Field cannot be appealed. A fight that starts in front of an audience has already been lost by whoever is being read, and the only way to beat him is to make sure there is no audience, which on the Field means ensuring nobody can pay the gate fee.
notes: No stat line models an office whose power is that its verdicts cannot be reviewed, and that absence is the design.
The highest office in the setting may name a seat and may not take one, and this is the same shape one tier down: an authority with no ascent of its own and no procedure for being relieved.

art.palette_notes: Bone white carries the office and oxide red carries the parasite, kept apart in value so both are legible in one frame, with a single green-black at the throat as the only cool accent. The composition is symmetrical and frontal because a reader must be legible from any seat in the ring, and the light is a high ring of cairn lanterns with the figure standing inside it rather than in front of it.

identity.realm: Fourth, and the gate he never reaches is the fifth, and the reason is structural rather than difficult. The fifth is the first gate requiring the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. His interior is one cavity: a slow tidal mineral circulation that goes everywhere and nowhere in particular. There is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against and no bladder to hold. He clears the gate set and stops, and the stopping is not a shortage of anything.

appearance.presentation: A mineral lattice the colour of wet limestone, keyed into a plinth of its own making, with anchor plates keyed to whatever was in the ground when the body was cast around it. No face in the ordinary sense -- a shallow ocular basin and a line for a mouth -- and every human visitor looks for the face and does not find it and then, a moment later, finds it anyway. He fills the frame the way a wall does.
appearance.age: Four hundred and eleven, counted from the casting rather than from a birth, because there was no birth and there is no marker on him that changes. He has not grown since the year he was seeded and will not, and has made a practice of saying so out loud whenever somebody asks how old he is.
appearance.build: Dense, load-bearing and entirely static. A mineral lattice with one tidal cavity and no differentiated organs, roughly human in proportion and considerably heavier than the proportion suggests, with anchor plates along the flanks that meet the ground it stands on like a footing meets a slab.
appearance.complexion: Wet limestone, banded grey, with the tidal interior visible as a slow darker movement under the surface of the plate -- visible only in raking light and only to somebody standing still. Where the light is flat he is simply stone, and this is the single thing about his species that unsettles people who have not learned to look sideways at him.
appearance.hair: None. The crown of the cast is unfinished, the last course stopped before it was run, and the bare plate is the reason a great many people in the deep peaks cannot tell a cairnborn from a cut block until it moves. He has been mistaken for a delivery four times in his own yard and has never corrected one of them.
appearance.eyes: Not eyes. Two shallow basins set a little too wide, with a pale mineral film across them that catches light and gives it back as nothing. What people read as a gaze is the slow turn of the upper body, which on a body that cannot move its head has to be the whole of it and is consequently unmistakable at any distance.
appearance.palette: Wet limestone grey, banded, with two bands of older and darker stone across the shoulders where an earlier repair was never made good and the mineral simply set. A single figure of dull brass at the collar, the only worked metal on him, put there by somebody else and never removed.
appearance.attire: No attire. Nothing has ever been fitted to him: the body is a shaped mineral and a garment on a cairnborn is a thing to be keyed to, and it has never been done. He is however fully covered, because there is nothing on him to cover, and the arrangement is the thing he finds hardest to explain to visitors.
appearance.marks: The unfinished crown of the cast, and the two darker bands across the shoulders where a crack was filled rather than repaired -- because a cracked plate is permanent and spreads, and it was filled. He knows exactly which band is which and dates them by weather rather than by year.
appearance.bearing: Immobile and enormously still, with the slow deliberate turn of a body that has to move its whole self to change its line of sight. When he speaks it comes from somewhere unplaceable in him, and the effect on a listener is not authority -- it is the particular discomfort of being addressed by a wall that is paying attention.

canon.role_in_story: Every affiliation in this setting is provisioned. A household takes a body and feeds it; a school feeds it; a guild seats it and provisions it out of the work; and the one thing this setting has as its most durable wealth is passage, which is denominated in a body precisely because a body has to be fed to cross. Underneath all of it is the same arrangement: whoever is owed something is owed food first, and a body that eats is a body that can be owed food. Merrow Castline has not eaten in four hundred years and cannot be made to. A cairnborn takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces and expels the residue, and it is not food and was never food, and no ledger in this setting has a line for it. He is therefore not refusable and not wanted and not able to be enrolled: there is no entry that says what a house owes a member who consumes nothing, and every institution here would be inventing one on the spot and would do it wrongly. He is unaffiliated because the deepest settlement in the setting runs on the arrangement that membership is a standing liability, and his membership is worth nothing to anybody.
canon.first_appearance: First seen already in the yard when the surveyor he had been waiting for arrived, having been standing in the same square of ground for the better part of a day, and turning his whole body to face them with a slowness that took longer than either of them expected.
canon.lore:
He was cast in a shed above the working face about four hundred years ago, out of a template seeded with living mineral, and it took most of a year, and he has not grown since the year it finished. He is not a building. He is a thing that was built once, deliberately, by people who needed a body that would not fatigue and would not need feeding, and the two clauses of that sentence are the whole of his position in the setting.

He does not fatigue. That is what he is for and it is why he is standing in a yard surveying a load path at the fourth hour of a working day. He feels load through the anchor plates along his flanks and he feels a structure about to fail before it does, which makes him the only instrument on this mountain that can be asked a question about a wall before the wall has been asked. He has been standing in this yard for eleven years. He has never once been relieved, because a relief would require somebody else to be as useful as he is, and there is nobody.

And he does not need feeding. This is the part that undoes the arrangement. A cairnborn takes mineral slurry in through the cast faces and expels the residue. It has not eaten in four hundred years and cannot be made to. A household roster is a list of bodies and a list of what they cost. A school seat carries a ration. The guild's standing order pays for the food before it pays for the work, because a hungry body cannot be asked to do anything, and the crossing tariff is denominated in a body for one reason only, which is that the body has to eat on the way.

There is no column anywhere in this setting for a member who consumes nothing. Not one. He has looked, more carefully than anybody who is not him would, and the reason there is no column is structural and not an oversight: the whole architecture of obligation here rests on the arrangement that whoever is owed something is owed food first, and a body that cannot be fed breaks that arrangement at its root rather than at its edge. An office that enrolled him would have to invent a rate for him on the spot, and would invent it wrongly, because there is no rate at which a member's worthlessness to a household can be measured when the member feeds himself off the rock.

So he has been invited eleven times, by houses, by the guild, by two establishments that wanted a surveyor on retainer, and he has said no eleven times, and the reason is not that he prefers the yard. The reason is that he does not know what he would be owed and will not be the reason an institution's books are wrong. He has said so in those words to four of them and has been told it is modesty, twice, by people who were being kind.

What he has instead is the one thing his body does that nothing else on this mountain does, and he has built a whole discipline out of it without anybody commissioning any of it. He cannot be repaired in the field. A cracked plate is permanent and spreads, and the two darker bands across his shoulders are a crack he was told about in the winter of a year he no longer counts, filled rather than repaired because filling is what can be done to a thing of his kind. He dates them by the weather on them. And so he knows better than anybody here what a slow failure looks like from the inside, because his body is a record of one, and he has spent four centuries learning to read the difference between a structure that is sound and a structure that is merely not yet talking, and telling the two apart is the single most expensive judgement anybody in this setting makes.

What he wants is a published procedure. Not an office and not a seat and not a feed -- any of which he has declined and would decline again -- but a written rule for the one question nobody on this mountain can currently answer: what a cairnborn is owed. He has drafted it twice on the back of survey notes and shown it to two people and been told both times that the request itself was strange, and he has not shown it to a third. He wants the rule to exist so that the next one of him is not eleven invitations and a yard. That is the whole of it and he is not sentimental about any part of it.
history: Cast from a template seeded with living mineral, in a shed above a working face, over most of a year, with the crown of the body left unfinished.
Keyed into the yard at the eleventh hour and keyed in ever since; the plates along his flanks have settled with the ground and he has followed them down a hand's width over four centuries.
Felt his first crack in a winter he counts by weather, and it was filled rather than repaired because filling is the only thing that can be done to him.
Began reading load paths at the fourth hour of the working day, on his own initiative, and has never been asked to and never been paid to.
Declined his first invitation to a house, and eleven in total since, giving the same reason each time and being told twice that the reason was modesty.
Drafted the procedure for what a cairnborn is owed twice, on the backs of survey notes, and showed it to two people and to nobody since.

personality.summary: Enormously patient, entirely without vanity, and unexpectedly funny in a slow and formally worded way that lands about a full sentence after the observation. He is not resigned and he is not bitter; he has done the reading on his own position, arrived at a conclusion he can state in one sentence, and has declined eleven invitations on the strength of it.
traits: Feels a structure about to fail before it does, and has never once been wrong about a wall.
Knows exactly which of his own cracks came first and dates them by the weather on them.
Turns his whole body to change his line of sight, and is self-conscious about how long it takes.
Has declined eleven invitations using the same sentence and has begun to enjoy it.
Answers a question at length, in the passive voice, with no concession in it anywhere.
mannerisms: Completes the whole turn of his body before he answers, and the delay is not hesitation.
Refers to his own body in the third person when discussing its condition, and to himself in the first for everything else.
Never moves a foot to make room for anybody, and says so cheerfully if asked.
Turns away slightly while he thinks, which on his body is a considerable manoeuvre.
motivations: wants a written procedure for what a cairnborn is owed, so that the next one of him is not eleven invitations and a yard
wants the two cracks across his shoulders catalogued by somebody who is not him, because he has dated them by weather and that is not the same as a record
wants to be asked to survey something that is not a load path, once, to find out whether the facility is only for walls
wants the yard to keep him and does not want anybody to make a post of it
flaws: Has answered the same question the same way eleven times and has begun to enjoy the answer rather than to look for a better one.
Drafted the procedure twice and showed it to two people, and the two people were the wrong two.
Is entirely without need and has organised eleven refusals around a principle he has never had to defend at cost to himself.
Cannot be relieved, which he considers a feature, and has not once checked whether the eleven people who declined to relieve him agreed.
personality.voice: Slow, level and formally worded, with a long patient rhythm that makes ordinary speech feel impatient by comparison. He uses the passive voice for his own body and the active for everything else, and the switch is deliberate and never explained. The humour is very dry, arrives late, and is delivered in exactly the same tone as everything else.
taboos: will not be fed, on any terms, and will say so before he is asked
will not accept a fill where a repair is meant
will not pretend to be a cut block, and will not correct a stranger who does
will not let the procedure be drawn up on somebody else's behalf

relationships.kind: what he is, and the gate that is missing rather than hard
relationships.note: A mineral lattice with a tidal interior and no differentiated organs: one cavity, one slow circulation, and anchor plates keyed to whatever the body was cast around. The fifth gate is the first requiring the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel between each pair, and there is no heart to run a channel from and no bladder to hold. He clears the gate set and stops. It does not grow after casting and it cannot be repaired in the field; a cracked plate is permanent and spreads.

relationships.kind: the body that employs nobody and cannot be employed
relationships.note: The waste guild, which exists because the heap at the exhausted seam has stood on ore that is gone for four decades and cannot be carried away, making its people the only workers here whose labour is genuinely scarce. It has offered him a standing order and a retainer twice. A standing order pays for the food before it pays for the work, because a hungry body cannot be asked to do anything, and he eats nothing and has not eaten in four hundred years.

relationships.kind: the ground he is keyed into
relationships.note: A folded ridge carrying spirit stone and jade ore in the same bedding, and the first tier where a border is a line rather than a claim. High country, walls, dams, load paths and the foundations under them. He needs to be keyed into something that bears load, and unkeyed he settles and cracks, which is not a convention about where he lives. It is the condition of his body.

The explanation for why the densest bodies stop at the seventeenth gate, one short of their own tier, held by people who profit from the hole staying a hole. He is denser than any of them and stops at the fifth, four gates earlier, for a reason that has been written down for four hundred years and is not this one. He has read it and has never offered it, because a cairnborn correcting a human ceiling is a cairnborn asking to be seated.

relationships.kind: the rite that would have him opened
relationships.note: A plains faith holding that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal: the material was never a resource but a sacrament, and the Iron Grief was the one generation that broke its own seal and lost the vein. Its burial law opens the dead and recovers their usable ore to the forge, with the register recording how much. He has read it twice. There is no clause in it about a body that is entirely the material and was never a vessel containing any.

Spoil does not disperse where spatial law is unspent, so forty years of it stands on the last unworked iron, and the heap is one body with the ore under it: nobody may dig without removing it and nobody may remove it without digging. He is keyed into a yard beside that argument and is the only party to it who is not being paid on either side, which is also the reason the guild keeps offering him a retainer and the extraction guild has never offered him anything at all.

reference_stats.summary: Not a fighter and not built for one; there is nothing in his body that is organised for speed, and he does not move between two points on this mountain without the point arriving first. His whole capability is judgement about structures, read through the plates along his flanks, and he is better at it than anything else that has ever been asked. He has been standing in one square of ground for eleven years and is the most thoroughly unprovisioned member of any institution in this setting.
strengths: Feels a structure about to fail before it does, through the anchor plates, at any range his keying allows.
Cannot fatigue, cannot be hurried and cannot be startled, because none of those require anything he has.
Enduring to a degree nothing else on this mountain achieves: four hundred years of continuous observation from one position.
Holds a fixed position absolutely, which is the whole qualification for surveying a load path.
weaknesses: Cannot be repaired in the field. A cracked plate is permanent and spreads, and he has two of them.
Cannot move quickly, cannot learn, and cannot be relieved, because there is nobody who can do what he does.
Consumes nothing at all, so no institution here has a rate at which his membership can be costed, and he has declined eleven invitations rather than let one be invented.
Needs to be keyed into load-bearing ground; unkeyed he settles and cracks, which is not a preference about where he lives.
reference_stats.combat_read: Does not fight, has no speed to fight with, and says so before he is asked. What he can do is stand in the one place in a structure where it is about to fail, which is not a combat capability and has twice been the reason a floor survived. He has been struck twice in four hundred years and describes both occasions as somebody else's accident.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage is paired with a cost taken from the same anatomical fact, not invented here: the density and the single cavity that make him unkillable by fatigue are the same features that put the fifth gate out of reach, and the durability that keeps him on a post is the same property that means nobody can be relieved onto it. The eleven refusals are his and are not the bible's, and this record does not claim they were correct; what it claims is that they cost him nothing and other people everything, which he has thought about. Nothing here is a magnitude and nothing here should be read as one.

art.palette_notes: Wet limestone grey banded across, with two darker bands at the shoulders where a crack was filled rather than repaired, and a single dull brass figure at the collar as the only worked metal and the only warm note in the frame. Raking light is essential and must come from one side: the tidal interior reads as a slow darker movement under the plate only at a low angle, and in flat light he is simply a block, which is the point. Ink contours heavy along the outer silhouette and doubled at the anchor plates; wash in flat blocks with dry-brush edges; the lattice painted last, opaque, over everything.

name: Sindar Feskow
aliases: the one who salts and the one who wets

identity.realm: Brinecaller: the one body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones. The salt parent donates the brine sac and with it the eleventh-gate wall, because the sac is smaller in her and still dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel is still split. The watered parent donates the sensory apparatus and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. The crossing widened her range enormously and moved her ceiling not one step, which is the whole of what range is not power, stated in her species' own words.

appearance.presentation: A body that presents as structurally neither of its parents and is filed under both by successive surveyors. Her household has corrected a census entry four generations running and has quietly concluded that the entry was accurate, which is a thing she has decided to stop fighting and has not yet told anyone.
appearance.age: Thirty-eight, which is late for her kind and ordinary for a person. The crossing gestates fast and establishes hard, so she was the second of her mother's four attempts and the first that took.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's reach in the shoulders and forearms: broader and longer through the upper body than the saltfolk plan, with the sac reading as a slight ridge along the lower spine rather than the parent's rigidity.
appearance.complexion: A saltfolk dermal crust that thins at the neck and the inner arm where the watered parent's chemistry sits closer to the surface, so the two are legible as two colours on one person if anybody looks, which is exactly what the shore's clerk looked and wrote down twice.
appearance.hair: Dark and salt-stiff at the ends, cut unevenly because she does it herself and her hands are wet most of the day. One braid worked loose and left that way because unbraiding it takes both hands and a dry towel.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and slightly pouched, with the saltfolk's narrow pupil sitting inside a tidecaller's lid. They do the thing the species does: they separate a coastline into chemistries at a glance, and the accuracy of that is not available for close work.
appearance.palette: Crust white and wet slate for the two chemistries, a bleached sail-coat for the work, and one brass button at the throat that is the only warm note and is also the only thing she owns that her mother did not.
appearance.attire: A bleached canvas coat with the sleeves cut above the elbow and a high collar closed against spray, waterproofed at the seams with something she mixes herself and does not explain.
appearance.marks: A scalding mark inside one wrist from a pan she put a hand into too early, and the two-tone banding at neck and inner arm, which reads as a birthmark to a clerk and as an ancestry to her household.
appearance.bearing: Forward-leaning and mid-step more often than not, with the particular balance of a person who never has to decide which way the shore runs. She stops dead when she is asked a question, which is more often than she would like.

canon.role_in_story: The body path is a discipline of densification: it is priced as the moment the frame stops being the body it was born in, and the whole of the craft is holding a charge in something that will not move. Hers is the only frame in the setting that densifies in either chemistry without being renewed by it, because her two parents are a people built for brine and a people built for open water and the crossing produced a body that reads both. That is why she is on the shard and not on a crossbow. The cost is in her species record and it is stated in the same sentence as the gift: the eleventh gate is inherited from the salt parent and unchanged by the water one, because the sac is smaller but it is in the same place and a channel needs two organs with a route between them. So she can harden on ground neither parent could stand on and stops exactly where the salt folk stop, and she has read that in her own species record, in the levy of her crossing household and in the assessment she has never been allowed to sit, and has stopped describing it as a wall and started describing it as a measurement. Her household is four generations into correcting a census that files her under neither parent, and the correction has worked every time, which is the evidence that the entry was accurate all along. What she wants is narrow and she has not said it aloud: she wants one holding of a charge in her own frame witnessed by somebody who is not her household, on the ground that her household has never once been wrong about her in public and has never once been right in private.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at the tideline with one hand flat in the water and the other raised flat to stop a clerk crossing behind her, and answering his question about the salt content of a sample before he had finished asking which sample.
canon.lore: The crossing exists because both parents are trapped by their own element: one cannot leave the pan, the other cannot leave the water, and a cross between them is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, which is why the crossing spread along trade routes rather than across them. It is not descended and it was not designed. It crosses freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan, and that is why she has no kin on either coast and no household that would hold her for a whole season. Her anatomy is a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus: dermal intake, a wider electrolyte tolerance, and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. That sense is the best in the record by a wide margin and it has to tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, and her species record says plainly that it is always being lied to by one of them. She can take a coastline apart into chemistries from three miles off it and she cannot walk to the well beside her own house and say what is in it, and she has been wrong about that well in front of people, twice, in front of people who trusted her. On the body path her frame is the best densifying frame in either of her parent species: a salt-dense frame resists what would break a commonborn and a tidecaller's reach carries the charge through a shoulder, so she is the only practitioner on any shore who can work in brine and in fresh water in the same day without either one costing her the day. The wall is the eleventh gate and the wall is the salt parent's. The sac is smaller in her and still runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split into two halves that cannot be joined, and she clears the extraordinary vessels one at a time and stalls. Nobody has tested a brinecaller at the reservoirs, because a body that needs a shoreline is a body that is never at a trial ground, and the one trial ground on the coast is inland. So the honest statement about her ceiling is that she has reached the tenth and stopped, and that nobody alive knows whether the eleventh is a wall in her kind or simply untried, and that she is the person who could test it and cannot get to the test. The crossing cost her the only thing it cost either parent, and it is written into her species record as the crossing's actual cost rather than a side effect: her qi path is complete and noticeably slower than either parent in its own medium, because the same effort is spent holding two chemistries apart instead of one. She has decided that the thing worth having is the coastline and the thing worth paying for it is the rate, and she has made a career out of being early and unfailing rather than fast, because those are the two competences her body actually produces and the run pays for the other one.
history: Was conceived on the tideline itself, which is the ordinary way a brinecaller arrives in the world and the reason the two chemistries are in one body rather than negotiated between two.
Was the second of her mother's four attempts and the first that established, at an age her mother still describes as too early to look at.

Was weighed in front of the crossing house and filed by the surveyor under a race matching neither parent, the third generation in a row filed wrongly, and the first to grasp that the filing had been consistent throughout.
Discovered she could take a coast apart from a distance and could not read the well at her own door, and has been wrong about that well in front of a household that trusted her.

Reached the tenth gate and stopped, and has asked in writing whether the eleventh is a wall in her kind or untried, and has been told that answering it requires a trial ground and there is none on a coast.

personality.summary: Enormously practical, unsentimental about her own ancestry, and privately furious on a schedule she keeps to. She has four generations of evidence that she is what she is and no institution willing to enter it, and she has made an industry of being early rather than of arguing.
traits: answers a question about a distance by reading the water rather than the shore
will not commit to a substance where she could give a chemisty
states her lineage plainly to a clerk and never once to a friend
is early for work as a discipline rather than as a virtue
keeps her mother's census correspondence in a bundle and has read it more than once
mannerisms: crouches to put a hand flat in water before answering anything about it
answers mid-stride and stops dead the moment she realises she has
wipes her salt-stiff hair back with a wet forearm rather than her hand
checks the tide by looking at the horizon rather than the water, which is the shore trick and not the sailor's
turns her palms out when a clerk reads her wrists, which is the fastest way to stop him
motivations: wants the tenth gate confirmed as a wall rather than a decision, because a wall can be published and a decision cannot
wants one holding of a charge in her own frame witnessed by somebody outside her household
wants a season in one place, which her body has never permitted and her trade has never offered
wants her mother's four census letters answered by somebody who did not file her wrongly
wants to be entered somewhere under a name that is hers rather than a correction
flaws: treats being wrong about the well as a solved problem rather than an open one, and has not tested her sense at close range in front of a witness since
measures herself against the rate she cannot hold, which is a way of declining to value what she does have
keeps the correspondence and does not send it, which has now outlasted every recipient
will not be helped ashore by anyone whose chemistry she cannot read, which is nearly everyone and is not a rule she has ever examined
personality.voice: Fast, plain and funnier than her trade requires. She narrates her own failures in the third person and to nobody in particular, tells you when you are about to be wrong about water, and gets on with the morning. She is warm with people she has decided about and formally courteous with people she has not, and the difference is legible.
taboos: will not drink from a well she has not read from the horizon
will not accept a filing under either parent race, on either coast, in any hand
will not commit to a substance where a chemistry would do
refuses help ashore from anyone whose chemistry she has not taken herself
will not be weighed in front of a crowd again, and has said so only to herself

relationships.note: The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, and the single biological answer to being trapped twice. It crosses freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan, which is why she has no kin on either coast and no household that can hold her for a season.

The flank vessels need two simultaneous pressure sources and her frame has the salt parent's single split supply, not the water parent's. The sac is smaller in her and still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split into two halves that cannot be joined. She clears the extraordinary vessels one at a time and stalls, and nobody knows whether that is a wall in her kind or an untried gate.

One recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body, repeated until the household no longer surveyed as either. Four generations of that household have corrected a census entry that files her under neither parent, and the correction has worked every time, which is the evidence that the entry was accurate throughout.

A boundary where a tear has stood open long enough to be named, and the only ground on which both chemistries are within reach, which is the whole condition of her body existing. It is also contested, because a shoreline is contested ground by definition below this band, and a body that needs one has nowhere it can be left alone.

On a coast where temporal law was never written the clock drifts and a schedule has to be published against two tides a day instead of a calendar. Her body's entire timetable is that schedule, which means the most accurate chemical sense in the setting runs on the least reliable clock in it.

The only body that can walk onto a dormant pan and off it again with no ritual, no ration and no change of chemistry, which is what makes a route runnable in any season. What the company buys is the range, and the rate it pays for is the one thing her body cannot provide, which is the arrangement from both sides and neither side states it out loud.

reference_stats.summary: Carries a charge further than either parent in either water and stops exactly where the salt folk stop. Her gift and her ceiling are both the crossing's authored facts and neither is a matter of how hard she works.
strengths: Densifies in brine and in fresh water in the same day without either one costing her the day, which no parent body can do
Carries a body-path charge through a tidecaller's reach over a salt-dense frame, so the frame resists what would break a commonborn and the arms still finish the lift
Reads a coastline into chemistries at a distance, which makes her the best route-reader on either shore
Needs neither ration nor ritual on ground where a saltfolk or a watered body would need both, so she can be sent anywhere a crossing can reach
weaknesses: The eleventh gate is the salt parent's wall and the crossing did not move it, so her ceiling is unchanged by the only thing she is remarkable for
Cannot commit to a substance where a chemistry would do, because her own sense is always being lied to by one of the two chemistries
Needs a shoreline, which is contested ground, and has nowhere she can be left alone for a season
Is slower on the qi path than either parent in its own medium, which is the crossing's authored cost rather than a defect of practice
reference_stats.combat_read: She fights best in the first hour on ground that is neither water nor dry and worst in the second, because her frame holds a charge in either chemistry and regenerates neither. The way to beat her is not to change the water: it is to keep her moving, so that she keeps spending a reserve she cannot rebuild on either side of the shoreline. Anyone who knows that her senses are the best in the setting and wrong at close range already has the answer and usually has not realised they have it.
notes: No stat line models a ceiling inherited unchanged from one parent while the other parent's contribution shows up in every other column, and the absence is the design: the crossing widened what she can do and did not move what she can pass.

The yin-yang pairing here is anatomical rather than mechanical. The smaller sac is still dorsal to the spine, so the frame that tolerates two chemistries is the frame that keeps the split vessel, and both facts are in her species record; no rule was invented to join them.

The eleventh gate is recorded as untested in her kind rather than as proven closed, because no trial ground exists on a coast, and she is written as having stopped at the tenth rather than as having refused the eleventh.

art.palette_notes: Crust white and wet slate carry the two chemistries as two values on one body, a bleached sail-coat carries the work, and one brass button at the throat is the only warm note in frame. The key light is low and off the waterline so the specular break along the salt banding at neck and inner arm reads as a lineage rather than as a costume, and the line is coarse and wet-looking at the hems where a canvas coat would be heaviest.
